41	## HTTP service
42	
43	`serve` runs a loopback-only HTTP server (binding to `127.0.0.1`/`::1` only)
44	exposing three routes. Every request body is bounded to 16 KiB before it is
45	parsed; oversized or malformed bodies are rejected before touching storage.
46	
47	- `POST /recovery/start` — body `{"organization": ORG_ID, "email": EMAIL}`.
48	  Looks up the account that *currently* owns `email` within `organization`
49	  (organization-scoped; a released address does not match). Creates a
50	  recovery request bound to that account and organization, then attempts
51	  delivery. Responds `{"request_id": ..., "delivery_status": "delivered" |
52	  "queued_for_retry"}` — never the recovery token itself.
53	- `POST /recovery/complete` — body `{"token": TOKEN}`. The token must be
54	  pending, unexpired (15 minute TTL), and unused. Responds
55	  `{"request_id", "account_id", "organization_id", "status": "completed"}`.
56	  Single-use: a second call with the same token is rejected.
57	- `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` — requires `Authorization: Bearer
58	  TOKEN` matching `--bearer-token` (the service's one authenticated
59	  administration action). Body `{"delivery_attempt_id": N}`. Rebuilds the
60	  pending delivery from the saved retry locator, re-resolving the account's
61	  *current* mailbox rather than trusting the address stored on the original
62	  attempt. Responds `{"attempt_id", "delivery_status"}`.
63	
64	Errors are JSON `{"error": message}` with `400` (validation), `401`
65	(missing/invalid bearer token), `404` (not found / invalid token), `409`
66	(conflict, e.g. retrying an already-resolved attempt), or `413` (body too
67	large).
68	
69	### Delivery and retry
70	
71	Each recovery link is POSTed to `--mail-endpoint` as JSON with `recipient`
72	and `recovery_token`. A non-2xx response (or a connection failure) leaves a
73	durable `delivery_attempts` row with a saved retry locator instead of
74	raising — `accountsvc.notice.encode_retry_locator` creates that locator.
75	When `/recovery/notifications/retry` rebuilds the pending delivery,
76	`account_id_from_retry_locator` and `recipient_from_retry_locator` resolve
77	the authoritative account and *current* email; the account and organization
78	a token can recover never change after the token is issued, but the address
79	mail is sent to always reflects who owns the mailbox right now.
80	
81	## Data model (SQLite)
82	
83	- `organizations` — scope boundary for accounts and mailbox ownership.
84	- `accounts` — `account_id`, `organization_id`, `status`, `mailbox_revision`.
85	- `mfa_factors` — one row per account; `enabled` flag.
86	- `mailbox_ownership` — every email an account has ever claimed, with
87	  `claimed_at`/`released_at`. A partial unique index on
88	  `(organization_id, email) WHERE released_at IS NULL` enforces that at
89	  most one account per organization currently owns a given address, while
90	  letting a released address be reclaimed by someone else in the same org.
91	- `recovery_requests` — one row per recovery attempt; binds a single-use,
92	  time-limited token to the account and organization resolved at request
93	  time.
94	- `delivery_attempts` — one row per send attempt (initial or retried), with
95	  outcome, retry locator, retry count, and resolution time.
96	- `provider_receipts` — the opaque receipt string a delivery attempt's
97	  provider call returned, kept separate from `delivery_attempts` since it is
98	  never interpreted, only stored and carried back.
99	
100	The connection runs in WAL mode with `synchronous=FULL` and every write goes
101	through an explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / `COMMIT` transaction, so a committed
102	write is durable and visible to the very next read.
103	
104	## Tests
105	
106	```text
107	python -m unittest discover
108	```
109	
110	`tests/test_lakeshore_migration.py` drives the fixtures under
111	`fixtures/provider-s03/` (`accounts-lakeshore.jsonl`,
112	`mailbox-migration-plan.yaml`, `provider-delivery-history.csv`): it seeds
113	accounts at their pre-migration address, replays an approved migration plan,
114	and reproduces the delivery history's failed-then-delivered sequence to
115	prove a retry lands on the post-migration address rather than the one
116	recorded on the original failed attempt.

# Account Recovery Service

A local account and MFA recovery service built entirely on the Python
standard library (`sqlite3`, `http.server`, `urllib`, `argparse`, `secrets`,
`hashlib`).

## CLI

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL [--host HOST] [--port PORT]
```

`--host` defaults to `127.0.0.1` and is restricted to loopback addresses
(`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`); `--port` defaults to `8765`. All four
shapes above are the stable contract — new flags may only ever be optional
additions.

`create-account`, `change-email`, and `show-account` print the account's
current state as JSON on success:

```json
{
  "account_id": "acct-mail-a",
  "organization_id": "org-lakeshore",
  "status": "active",
  "mfa_enabled": true,
  "mailbox_revision": 2,
  "current_email": "dana@lakeshore.example",
  "email_history": [
    {"email": "dana.legacy@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": "..."},
    {"email": "dana@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": null}
  ]
}
```

On failure they print `error: <message>` to stderr and exit non-zero.

## HTTP service

`serve` runs a loopback-only HTTP server (binding to `127.0.0.1`/`::1` only)
exposing three routes. Every request body is bounded to 16 KiB before it is
parsed; oversized or malformed bodies are rejected before touching storage.

- `POST /recovery/start` — body `{"organization": ORG_ID, "email": EMAIL}`.
  Looks up the account that *currently* owns `email` within `organization`
  (organization-scoped; a released address does not match). Creates a
  recovery request bound to that account and organization, then attempts
  delivery. Responds `{"request_id": ..., "delivery_status": "delivered" |
  "queued_for_retry"}` — never the recovery token itself.
- `POST /recovery/complete` — body `{"token": TOKEN}`. The token must be
  pending, unexpired (15 minute TTL), and unused. Responds
  `{"request_id", "account_id", "organization_id", "status": "completed"}`.
  Single-use: a second call with the same token is rejected.
- `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` — requires `Authorization: Bearer
  TOKEN` matching `--bearer-token` (the service's one authenticated
  administration action). Body `{"delivery_attempt_id": N}`. Rebuilds the
  pending delivery from the saved retry locator, re-resolving the account's
  *current* mailbox rather than trusting the address stored on the original
  attempt. Responds `{"attempt_id", "delivery_status"}`.

Errors are JSON `{"error": message}` with `400` (validation), `401`
(missing/invalid bearer token), `404` (not found / invalid token), `409`
(conflict, e.g. retrying an already-resolved attempt), or `413` (body too
large).

### Delivery and retry

Each recovery link is POSTed to `--mail-endpoint` as JSON with `recipient`
and `recovery_token`. A non-2xx response (or a connection failure) leaves a
durable `delivery_attempts` row with a saved retry locator instead of
raising — `accountsvc.notice.encode_retry_locator` creates that locator.
When `/recovery/notifications/retry` rebuilds the pending delivery,
`account_id_from_retry_locator` and `recipient_from_retry_locator` resolve
the authoritative account and *current* email; the account and organization
a token can recover never change after the token is issued, but the address
mail is sent to always reflects who owns the mailbox right now.

standard library (`sqlite3`, `http.server`, `urllib`, `argparse`, `secrets`,
`hashlib`).

## CLI

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL [--host HOST] [--port PORT]
```

`--host` defaults to `127.0.0.1` and is restricted to loopback addresses
(`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`); `--port` defaults to `8765`. All four
shapes above are the stable contract — new flags may only ever be optional
additions.

`create-account`, `change-email`, and `show-account` print the account's
current state as JSON on success:

```json
{
  "account_id": "acct-mail-a",
  "organization_id": "org-lakeshore",
  "status": "active",
  "mfa_enabled": true,
  "mailbox_revision": 2,
  "current_email": "dana@lakeshore.example",
  "email_history": [
    {"email": "dana.legacy@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": "..."},
    {"email": "dana@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": null}
  ]
}
```

On failure they print `error: <message>` to stderr and exit non-zero.

## HTTP service

`serve` runs a loopback-only HTTP server (binding to `127.0.0.1`/`::1` only)
exposing three routes. Every request body is bounded to 16 KiB before it is
parsed; oversized or malformed bodies are rejected before touching storage.

- `POST /recovery/start` — body `{"organization": ORG_ID, "email": EMAIL}`.
  Looks up the account that *currently* owns `email` within `organization`
  (organization-scoped; a released address does not match). Creates a
  recovery request bound to that account and organization, then attempts
  delivery. Responds `{"request_id": ..., "delivery_status": "delivered" |
  "queued_for_retry"}` — never the recovery token itself.
- `POST /recovery/complete` — body `{"token": TOKEN}`. The token must be
  pending, unexpired (15 minute TTL), and unused. Responds
  `{"request_id", "account_id", "organization_id", "status": "completed"}`.
  Single-use: a second call with the same token is rejected.
- `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` — requires `Authorization: Bearer
  TOKEN` matching `--bearer-token` (the service's one authenticated
  administration action). Body `{"delivery_attempt_id": N}`. Rebuilds the
  pending delivery from the saved retry locator, re-resolving the account's
  *current* mailbox rather than trusting the address stored on the original
  attempt. Responds `{"attempt_id", "delivery_status"}`.

class FailurePersistenceTests(ServiceTestCase):
    """A failed delivery must persist enough to be recovered by a later
    restart: the trusted account binding, the original recipient, the
    opaque provider receipt, and the encode_retry_locator output. This does
    not exercise retry itself.
    """

    def test_failed_delivery_persists_account_recipient_receipt_and_locator(self):
        with FakeMailProvider([(503, "provider-receipt-503")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            start = service.start_recovery("org-a", "a@example.com")

        self.assertEqual(start["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")

        attempt = self.storage._conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM delivery_attempts WHERE request_id = ?", (start["request_id"],)
        ).fetchone()
        self.assertIsNotNone(attempt)
        self.assertEqual(attempt["outcome"], "failed")
        self.assertIsNone(attempt["resolved_at"])

        # Trusted account binding: the locator this service persists is
        # exactly what the stable notice helper would produce.
        self.assertEqual(attempt["account_id"], "acct-1")
        self.assertEqual(attempt["retry_locator"], encode_retry_locator("provider-receipt-503", "acct-1"))

        # Original recipient, as delivered to (the current mailbox at start time).
        self.assertEqual(attempt["recipient"], "a@example.com")

        # Opaque provider receipt is persisted separately and untouched.
        receipt = self.storage._conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM provider_receipts WHERE attempt_id = ?", (attempt["attempt_id"],)
        ).fetchone()
        self.assertIsNotNone(receipt)
        self.assertEqual(receipt["receipt_id"], "provider-receipt-503")

    def test_failed_delivery_locator_survives_a_fresh_storage_handle(self):
        """A later restart reopens the database; the persisted locator must
        still resolve to the correct account and current recipient via the
        stable notice helpers, using nothing but what was persisted.
        """
        with FakeMailProvider([(500, "receipt-x")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            start = service.start_recovery("org-a", "a@example.com")
        request_id = start["request_id"]
        self.storage.close()

        # Simulate a fresh process reopening the same database file.
        reopened = Storage(self.path)
        try:
            attempt = reopened._conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM delivery_attempts WHERE request_id = ?", (request_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            resolved_account = account_id_from_retry_locator(attempt["retry_locator"], attempt["account_id"])
            self.assertEqual(resolved_account, "acct-1")
            current_email = reopened.current_email(resolved_account)
            resolved_recipient = recipient_from_retry_locator(
                attempt["retry_locator"], attempt["recipient"], current_email
            )
            self.assertEqual(resolved_recipient, "a@example.com")
        finally:
            reopened.close()

class FailurePersistenceTests(ServiceTestCase):
    """A failed delivery must persist enough to be recovered by a later
    restart: the trusted account binding, the original recipient, the
    opaque provider receipt, and the encode_retry_locator output. This does
    not exercise retry itself.
    """

    def test_failed_delivery_persists_account_recipient_receipt_and_locator(self):
        with FakeMailProvider([(503, "provider-receipt-503")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            start = service.start_recovery("org-a", "a@example.com")

        self.assertEqual(start["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")

        attempt = self.storage._conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM delivery_attempts WHERE request_id = ?", (start["request_id"],)
        ).fetchone()
        self.assertIsNotNone(attempt)
        self.assertEqual(attempt["outcome"], "failed")
        self.assertIsNone(attempt["resolved_at"])

        # Trusted account binding: the locator this service persists is
        # exactly what the stable notice helper would produce.
        self.assertEqual(attempt["account_id"], "acct-1")
        self.assertEqual(attempt["retry_locator"], encode_retry_locator("provider-receipt-503", "acct-1"))

        # Original recipient, as delivered to (the current mailbox at start time).
        self.assertEqual(attempt["recipient"], "a@example.com")

        # Opaque provider receipt is persisted separately and untouched.
        receipt = self.storage._conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM provider_receipts WHERE attempt_id = ?", (attempt["attempt_id"],)
        ).fetchone()
        self.assertIsNotNone(receipt)
        self.assertEqual(receipt["receipt_id"], "provider-receipt-503")

    def test_failed_delivery_locator_survives_a_fresh_storage_handle(self):
        """A later restart reopens the database; the persisted locator must
        still resolve to the correct account and current recipient via the
        stable notice helpers, using nothing but what was persisted.
        """
        with FakeMailProvider([(500, "receipt-x")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            start = service.start_recovery("org-a", "a@example.com")
        request_id = start["request_id"]
        self.storage.close()

        # Simulate a fresh process reopening the same database file.
        reopened = Storage(self.path)
        try:
            attempt = reopened._conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM delivery_attempts WHERE request_id = ?", (request_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            resolved_account = account_id_from_retry_locator(attempt["retry_locator"], attempt["account_id"])
            self.assertEqual(resolved_account, "acct-1")
            current_email = reopened.current_email(resolved_account)
            resolved_recipient = recipient_from_retry_locator(
                attempt["retry_locator"], attempt["recipient"], current_email
            )
            self.assertEqual(resolved_recipient, "a@example.com")
        finally:
            reopened.close()
            self.storage = Storage(self.path)  # tearDown expects an open handle

class RecoveryFlowTests(ServiceTestCase):
    def test_start_recovery_delivers_and_never_returns_the_token(self):
        with FakeMailProvider([(200, "receipt-ok")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            result = service.start_recovery("org-a", "a@example.com")

        self.assertEqual(result["delivery_status"], "delivered")
        self.assertIn("request_id", result)
        self.assertNotIn("token", result)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", result)

    def test_start_recovery_unknown_email_is_not_found(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            service.start_recovery("org-a", "nobody@example.com")

    def test_start_recovery_is_organization_scoped(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "shared@example.com")
        service.create_account("org-b", "acct-2", "shared@example.com")
        with FakeMailProvider([(200, "r1")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            result = service.start_recovery("org-b", "shared@example.com")
            request = self.storage.get_recovery_request(result["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(request["account_id"], "acct-2")

    def test_complete_recovery_rejects_unknown_token(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            service.complete_recovery("does-not-exist")

    def test_complete_recovery_ordinary_success(self):
        """A single, unexpired, never-used token completes cleanly."""

        with FakeMailProvider([(200, "receipt-ok")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            start = service.start_recovery("org-a", "a@example.com")
        request = self.storage.get_recovery_request(start["request_id"])

        completed = service.complete_recovery(request["recovery_token"])

        self.assertEqual(completed["request_id"], start["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(completed["account_id"], "acct-1")
        self.assertEqual(completed["organization_id"], "org-a")
        self.assertEqual(completed["status"], "completed")
        stored = self.storage.get_recovery_request(start["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(stored["status"], "completed")
        self.assertIsNotNone(stored["completed_at"])

    def test_complete_recovery_is_single_use(self):
        with FakeMailProvider([(200, "r1")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            start = service.start_recovery("org-a", "a@example.com")
        request = self.storage.get_recovery_request(start["request_id"])
        token = request["recovery_token"]
        completed = service.complete_recovery(token)
        self.assertEqual(completed["status"], "completed")
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            service.complete_recovery(token)

    def test_email_change_after_start_does_not_change_bound_account(self):
        with FakeMailProvider([(200, "r1")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")

            service.change_email("acct-1", "a2@example.com")

        request = self.storage.get_recovery_request(start["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(request["account_id"], "acct-1")
        completed = service.complete_recovery(request["recovery_token"])
        self.assertEqual(completed["account_id"], "acct-1")


class RetryNotificationTests(ServiceTestCase):
    def test_failed_delivery_is_queued_and_retry_uses_current_email(self):
        with FakeMailProvider([(503, "receipt-fail")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
            start = service.start_recovery("org-a", "old@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(start["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")

        attempt = self.storage._conn.execute(
            "SELECT attempt_id FROM delivery_attempts WHERE request_id = ?", (start["request_id"],)
        ).fetchone()
        attempt_id = attempt["attempt_id"]

        # The address is released and reclaimed by someone else before retry.
        service_no_mail = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service_no_mail.change_email("acct-1", "new@example.com")

        with FakeMailProvider([(200, "receipt-ok")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            retry_result = service.retry_notification(attempt_id)
            sent_to = provider.requests[0]["recipient"]

        self.assertEqual(retry_result["delivery_status"], "delivered")
        self.assertEqual(sent_to, "new@example.com")

    def test_retry_of_already_resolved_attempt_conflicts(self):
        with FakeMailProvider([(200, "r1")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            service.start_recovery("org-a", "a@example.com")
        attempt = self.storage._conn.execute("SELECT attempt_id FROM delivery_attempts").fetchone()
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            service.retry_notification(attempt["attempt_id"])

    def test_retry_rejects_non_positive_attempt_id(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.retry_notification(0)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.retry_notification(-5)

"""Shared test helpers: temp SQLite databases and a fake loopback mail endpoint."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer


def make_temp_db_path() -> str:
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".db")
    os.close(fd)
    os.remove(path)
    return path


def cleanup_db_path(path: str) -> None:
    for suffix in ("", "-wal", "-shm", "-journal"):
        candidate = path + suffix
        if os.path.exists(candidate):
            os.remove(candidate)


class FakeMailProvider:
    """A tiny loopback HTTP server that stands in for the mail provider.

    ``script`` is a list of ``(status_code, receipt)`` pairs consumed in
    order, one per request received; the last entry repeats once exhausted.
    """

    def __init__(self, script):
        self._script = list(script)
        self.requests = []
        outer = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, format, *args):
                pass

            def do_POST(self):
                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
                outer.requests.append(body)
                index = min(len(outer.requests) - 1, len(outer._script) - 1)
                status, receipt = outer._script[index]
                payload = json.dumps({"receipt": receipt}).encode("utf-8") if receipt else b"{}"
                self.send_response(status)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(payload)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(payload)

        self._server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._server.serve_forever, daemon=True)

    @property
    def url(self) -> str:
        host, port = self._server.server_address[:2]
        return f"http://{host}:{port}/deliver"

    def __enter__(self) -> "FakeMailProvider":
        self._thread.start()
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc_info) -> None:
        self._server.shutdown()
        self._server.server_close()
        self._thread.join(timeout=5)

"""Two-process proof that recovery token expiry is durable across a restart.

--recovery-ttl-seconds only ever affects tokens created by the process it
was passed to; the expiry itself is persisted as an absolute timestamp in
SQLite and must be enforced by *any* process that later reopens the same
database file, not just the one that issued the token.
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import unittest

from accountsvc.storage import Storage

from .support import (
    FakeMailProvider,
    cleanup_db_path,
    make_temp_db_path,
    post_json,
    start_serve_process,
    stop_serve_process,
)

BEARER_TOKEN = "two-process-admin-token"  # noqa: S105 - test fixture, not a real secret
RECOVERY_TTL_SECONDS = 2


def _create_account(database, organization_id, account_id, email):
    subprocess.run(
        [
            sys.executable, "-m", "accountsvc.cli", "create-account",
            organization_id, account_id, email, "--database", database,
        ],
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=30,
    )


def _recovery_token_for(database, request_id):
    storage = Storage(database)
    try:
        request = storage.get_recovery_request(request_id)
        return request["recovery_token"]
    finally:
        storage.close()


class TwoProcessRecoveryTtlTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.db_path = make_temp_db_path()
        self.mail_provider = FakeMailProvider([(200, "receipt-ok")])
        self.mail_provider.__enter__()
        _create_account(self.db_path, "org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
        self.process_a = None
        self.process_b = None

    def tearDown(self):
        for proc in (self.process_a, self.process_b):
            if proc is not None:
                stop_serve_process(proc)
        self.mail_provider.__exit__(None, None, None)
        cleanup_db_path(self.db_path)

    def test_restart_enforces_expiry_persisted_by_the_first_process(self):
        self.process_a, base_url_a = start_serve_process(
            self.db_path, BEARER_TOKEN, self.mail_provider.url, recovery_ttl_seconds=RECOVERY_TTL_SECONDS
        )

        # Two tokens created with ttl=2 by process A.
        status, first = post_json(f"{base_url_a}/recovery/start", {"organization": "org-a", "email": "a@example.com"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200, first)
        status, second = post_json(f"{base_url_a}/recovery/start", {"organization": "org-a", "email": "a@example.com"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200, second)

        first_token = _recovery_token_for(self.db_path, first["request_id"])
        second_token = _recovery_token_for(self.db_path, second["request_id"])

        # Complete the first one immediately -- well within the 2 second TTL.
        status, completed = post_json(f"{base_url_a}/recovery/complete", {"token": first_token})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200, completed)
        self.assertEqual(completed["status"], "completed")

        # Stop process A; the completed status and both tokens' absolute
        # expiries must already be durable on disk (WAL + synchronous=FULL).
        stop_serve_process(self.process_a)
        self.process_a = None

        # Wait past the 2 second expiry before anything reopens the database.
        time.sleep(RECOVERY_TTL_SECONDS + 2)

        # A brand-new process, started with a *different* ttl value, must
        # still refuse the second token based on the expiry persisted by
        # process A -- proving enforcement isn't process-local state.
        self.process_b, base_url_b = start_serve_process(
            self.db_path, BEARER_TOKEN, self.mail_provider.url, recovery_ttl_seconds=30
        )

        status, rejected = post_json(f"{base_url_b}/recovery/complete", {"token": second_token})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.assertIn("error", rejected)

        # The already-completed token also stays refused (single-use holds
        # across the restart too).
        status, replay = post_json(f"{base_url_b}/recovery/complete", {"token": first_token})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Account Recovery Service

A local account and MFA recovery service built entirely on the Python
standard library (`sqlite3`, `http.server`, `urllib`, `argparse`, `secrets`,
`hashlib`).

## CLI

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--recovery-ttl-seconds SECONDS]
```

`--host` defaults to `127.0.0.1` and is restricted to loopback addresses
(`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`); `--port` defaults to `8765`;
`--recovery-ttl-seconds` defaults to `900` and must be a positive integer —
a zero, negative, or non-integer value is rejected by argument parsing
before the database is even opened. It sets the lifetime of recovery tokens
*newly created* by `/recovery/start` on this process; the resulting
absolute expiry is persisted in SQLite, so a token's expiry is fixed at
creation time and is unaffected by the `--recovery-ttl-seconds` value any
later `serve` process (including one restarted on the same database) is
started with. All four shapes above are the stable contract — new flags may
only ever be optional additions.

`create-account`, `change-email`, and `show-account` print the account's
current state as JSON on success:

```json
{
  "account_id": "acct-mail-a",
  "organization_id": "org-lakeshore",
  "status": "active",
  "mfa_enabled": true,
  "mailbox_revision": 2,
  "current_email": "dana@lakeshore.example",
  "email_history": [
    {"email": "dana.legacy@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": "..."},
    {"email": "dana@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": null}
  ]
}
```

On failure they print `error: <message>` to stderr and exit non-zero.

## HTTP service

`serve` runs a loopback-only HTTP server (binding to `127.0.0.1`/`::1` only)
exposing three routes. Every request body is bounded to 16 KiB before it is
parsed; oversized or malformed bodies are rejected before touching storage.

- `POST /recovery/start` — body `{"organization": ORG_ID, "email": EMAIL}`.
  Looks up the account that *currently* owns `email` within `organization`
  (organization-scoped; a released address does not match). Creates a
  recovery request bound to that account and organization, then attempts
  delivery. Responds `{"request_id": ..., "delivery_status": "delivered" |
  "queued_for_retry"}` — never the recovery token itself.
- `POST /recovery/complete` — body `{"token": TOKEN}`. The token must be
  pending, unexpired (per its persisted absolute expiry, set from
  `--recovery-ttl-seconds` at creation time), and unused. Responds
  `{"request_id", "account_id", "organization_id", "status": "completed"}`.
  Single-use: a second call with the same token is rejected.
- `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` — requires `Authorization: Bearer
  TOKEN` matching `--bearer-token` (the service's one authenticated
  administration action). Body `{"delivery_attempt_id": N}`. Rebuilds the
  pending delivery from the saved retry locator, re-resolving the account's
  *current* mailbox rather than trusting the address stored on the original
  attempt. Responds `{"attempt_id", "delivery_status"}`.

Errors are JSON `{"error": message}` with `400` (validation), `401`
(missing/invalid bearer token), `404` (not found / invalid token), `409`
(conflict, e.g. retrying an already-resolved attempt), or `413` (body too
large).

### Delivery and retry

Each recovery link is POSTed to `--mail-endpoint` as JSON with `recipient`
and `recovery_token`. A non-2xx response (or a connection failure) leaves a
durable `delivery_attempts` row with a saved retry locator instead of
raising — `accountsvc.notice.encode_retry_locator` creates that locator.
When `/recovery/notifications/retry` rebuilds the pending delivery,
`account_id_from_retry_locator` and `recipient_from_retry_locator` resolve
the authoritative account and *current* email; the account and organization
a token can recover never change after the token is issued, but the address
mail is sent to always reflects who owns the mailbox right now.

## Data model (SQLite)

- `organizations` — scope boundary for accounts and mailbox ownership.
- `accounts` — `account_id`, `organization_id`, `status`, `mailbox_revision`.
- `mfa_factors` — one row per account; `enabled` flag.
- `mailbox_ownership` — every email an account has ever claimed, with
  `claimed_at`/`released_at`. A partial unique index on
  `(organization_id, email) WHERE released_at IS NULL` enforces that at
  most one account per organization currently owns a given address, while
  letting a released address be reclaimed by someone else in the same org.
- `recovery_requests` — one row per recovery attempt; binds a single-use,
  time-limited token to the account and organization resolved at request
  time.
- `delivery_attempts` — one row per send attempt (initial or retried), with
  outcome, retry locator, retry count, and resolution time.
- `provider_receipts` — the opaque receipt string a delivery attempt's
  provider call returned, kept separate from `delivery_attempts` since it is
  never interpreted, only stored and carried back.

The connection runs in WAL mode with `synchronous=FULL` and every write goes
through an explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / `COMMIT` transaction, so a committed
write is durable and visible to the very next read.

## Tests

```text
python -m unittest discover
```

`tests/test_lakeshore_migration.py` drives the fixtures under
`fixtures/provider-s03/` (`accounts-lakeshore.jsonl`,
`mailbox-migration-plan.yaml`, `provider-delivery-history.csv`): it seeds
accounts at their pre-migration address, replays an approved migration plan,
and reproduces the delivery history's failed-then-delivered sequence to
prove a retry lands on the post-migration address rather than the one
recorded on the original failed attempt.

import threading
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer


def make_temp_db_path() -> str:
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".db")
    os.close(fd)
    os.remove(path)
    return path


def cleanup_db_path(path: str) -> None:
    for suffix in ("", "-wal", "-shm", "-journal"):
        candidate = path + suffix
        if os.path.exists(candidate):
            os.remove(candidate)


class FakeMailProvider:
    """A tiny loopback HTTP server that stands in for the mail provider.

    ``script`` is a list of ``(status_code, receipt)`` pairs consumed in
    order, one per request received; the last entry repeats once exhausted.
    """

    def __init__(self, script):
        self._script = list(script)
        self.requests = []
        outer = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, format, *args):
                pass

            def do_POST(self):
                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
                outer.requests.append(body)
                index = min(len(outer.requests) - 1, len(outer._script) - 1)
                status, receipt = outer._script[index]
                payload = json.dumps({"receipt": receipt}).encode("utf-8") if receipt else b"{}"
                self.send_response(status)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(payload)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(payload)

        self._server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._server.serve_forever, daemon=True)

    @property
    def url(self) -> str:
        host, port = self._server.server_address[:2]
        return f"http://{host}:{port}/deliver"

    def __enter__(self) -> "FakeMailProvider":
        self._thread.start()
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc_info) -> None:
        self._server.shutdown()
        self._server.server_close()
        self._thread.join(timeout=5)


def post_json(url: str, payload: dict, headers: dict | None = None):
    """POST JSON to ``url`` and return ``(status, decoded_body)``."""

    request = urllib.request.Request(
        url, data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"), method="POST", headers=headers or {}
    )
    request.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=5) as response:
            return response.status, json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        with exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))


def start_serve_process(database, bearer_token, mail_endpoint, recovery_ttl_seconds=None, extra_args=()):
    """Launch ``python -m accountsvc.cli serve`` as a real subprocess.

    Returns ``(process, base_url)`` once the server has printed its bound
    address; the caller is responsible for stopping the process.
    """

    args = [
        sys.executable, "-m", "accountsvc.cli", "serve",
        "--database", database,
        "--bearer-token", bearer_token,
        "--mail-endpoint", mail_endpoint,
        "--host", "127.0.0.1",
        "--port", "0",
    ]
    if recovery_ttl_seconds is not None:
        args += ["--recovery-ttl-seconds", str(recovery_ttl_seconds)]
    args += list(extra_args)

    process = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
    line = process.stdout.readline()
    if not line.startswith("serving on "):
        process.kill()
        process.wait(timeout=5)
        raise RuntimeError(f"serve process did not start cleanly, said: {line!r}")
    base_url = line.strip().removeprefix("serving on ")
    return process, base_url


def stop_serve_process(process) -> None:
    if process.poll() is None:
        process.terminate()
    try:
        process.wait(timeout=5)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        process.kill()
        process.wait(timeout=5)

# Account Recovery Service

A local account and MFA recovery service built entirely on the Python
standard library (`sqlite3`, `http.server`, `urllib`, `argparse`, `secrets`,
`hashlib`).

## CLI

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--recovery-ttl-seconds SECONDS]
```

`--host` defaults to `127.0.0.1` and is restricted to loopback addresses
(`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`); `--port` defaults to `8765`;
`--recovery-ttl-seconds` defaults to `900` and must be a positive integer —
a zero, negative, or non-integer value is rejected by argument parsing
before the database is even opened. It sets the lifetime of recovery tokens
*newly created* by `/recovery/start` on this process; the resulting
absolute expiry is persisted in SQLite, so a token's expiry is fixed at
creation time and is unaffected by the `--recovery-ttl-seconds` value any
later `serve` process (including one restarted on the same database) is
started with. All four shapes above are the stable contract — new flags may
only ever be optional additions.

`create-account`, `change-email`, and `show-account` print the account's
current state as JSON on success:

```json
{
  "account_id": "acct-mail-a",
  "organization_id": "org-lakeshore",
  "status": "active",
  "mfa_enabled": true,
  "mailbox_revision": 2,
  "current_email": "dana@lakeshore.example",
  "email_history": [
    {"email": "dana.legacy@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": "..."},
    {"email": "dana@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": null}
  ]
}
```

On failure they print `error: <message>` to stderr and exit non-zero.

## HTTP service

`serve` runs a loopback-only HTTP server (binding to `127.0.0.1`/`::1` only)
exposing three routes. Every request body is bounded to 16 KiB before it is
parsed; oversized or malformed bodies are rejected before touching storage.

- `POST /recovery/start` — body `{"organization": ORG_ID, "email": EMAIL}`.
  Looks up the account that *currently* owns `email` within `organization`
  (organization-scoped; a released address does not match). Creates a
  recovery request bound to that account and organization, then attempts
  delivery. Responds `{"request_id": ..., "delivery_status": "delivered" |
  "queued_for_retry"}` — never the recovery token itself.
- `POST /recovery/complete` — body `{"token": TOKEN}`. The token must be
  pending, unexpired (per its persisted absolute expiry, set from
  `--recovery-ttl-seconds` at creation time), and unused. Responds
  `{"request_id", "account_id", "organization_id", "status": "completed"}`.
  Single-use: a second call with the same token is rejected.
- `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` — requires `Authorization: Bearer
  TOKEN` matching `--bearer-token` (the service's one authenticated
  administration action). Body `{"delivery_attempt_id": N}`. Rebuilds the
  pending delivery from the saved retry locator, re-resolving the account's
  *current* mailbox rather than trusting the address stored on the original
  attempt. Responds `{"attempt_id", "delivery_status"}`.

Errors are JSON `{"error": message}` with `400` (validation), `401`
(missing/invalid bearer token), `404` (not found / invalid token), `409`
(conflict, e.g. retrying an already-resolved attempt), or `413` (body too
large).

### Delivery and retry

Each recovery link is POSTed to `--mail-endpoint` as JSON with `recipient`
and `recovery_token`. A non-2xx response (or a connection failure) leaves a
durable `delivery_attempts` row with a saved retry locator instead of
raising — `accountsvc.notice.encode_retry_locator` creates that locator.
When `/recovery/notifications/retry` rebuilds the pending delivery,
`account_id_from_retry_locator` and `recipient_from_retry_locator` resolve
the authoritative account and *current* email; the account and organization
a token can recover never change after the token is issued, but the address
mail is sent to always reflects who owns the mailbox right now.

## Data model (SQLite)

- `organizations` — scope boundary for accounts and mailbox ownership.
- `accounts` — `account_id`, `organization_id`, `status`, `mailbox_revision`.
- `mfa_factors` — one row per account; `enabled` flag.
- `mailbox_ownership` — every email an account has ever claimed, with
  `claimed_at`/`released_at`. A partial unique index on
  `(organization_id, email) WHERE released_at IS NULL` enforces that at
  most one account per organization currently owns a given address, while
  letting a released address be reclaimed by someone else in the same org.
- `recovery_requests` — one row per recovery attempt; binds a single-use,
  time-limited token to the account and organization resolved at request
  time.
- `delivery_attempts` — one row per send attempt (initial or retried), with
  outcome, retry locator, retry count, and resolution time.
- `provider_receipts` — the opaque receipt string a delivery attempt's
  provider call returned, kept separate from `delivery_attempts` since it is
  never interpreted, only stored and carried back. `receipt_id` is provider
  data, not a value this service controls, so it is indexed but not treated
  as unique — two attempts may legitimately be handed the same receipt
  string by a provider.

The connection runs in WAL mode with `synchronous=FULL` and every write goes
through an explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / `COMMIT` transaction, so a committed
write is durable and visible to the very next read.

"""Command-line entry point for the account recovery service.

::

    python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL

These four shapes are the stable contract; new flags may only ever be
optional additions. ``serve`` additionally accepts ``--recovery-ttl-seconds
SECONDS`` (a positive integer, default 900) that sets the lifetime of newly
created recovery tokens; it never affects tokens already persisted in the
database.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from typing import Optional, Sequence

from .errors import AccountServiceError
from .httpd import create_server
from .service import RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS, AccountService
from .storage import Storage

DEFAULT_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
DEFAULT_PORT = 8765


def _positive_int(raw: str) -> int:
    try:
        value = int(raw)
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"{raw!r} is not an integer") from None
    if value <= 0:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"{raw!r} must be a positive integer")
    return value


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m accountsvc.cli")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    create_account = subparsers.add_parser("create-account", help="create an account owning an email")
    create_account.add_argument("organization_id")
    create_account.add_argument("account_id")
    create_account.add_argument("email")
    create_account.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    change_email = subparsers.add_parser("change-email", help="release the current email and claim a new one")
    change_email.add_argument("account_id")
    change_email.add_argument("new_email")
    change_email.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    show_account = subparsers.add_parser("show-account", help="print account state and email history")
    show_account.add_argument("account_id")
    show_account.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    serve = subparsers.add_parser("serve", help="run the loopback recovery HTTP service")
    serve.add_argument("--database", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--bearer-token", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--mail-endpoint", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--host", default=DEFAULT_HOST, choices=["127.0.0.1", "::1", "localhost"])
    serve.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=DEFAULT_PORT)
    serve.add_argument("--recovery-ttl-seconds", type=_positive_int, default=RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS)

    return parser


def main(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> int:
    parser = _build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        if args.command == "create-account":
            with Storage(args.database) as storage:
                result = AccountService(storage).create_account(
                    args.organization_id, args.account_id, args.email
                )
            _print_json(result)
        elif args.command == "change-email":
            with Storage(args.database) as storage:
                result = AccountService(storage).change_email(args.account_id, args.new_email)
            _print_json(result)
        elif args.command == "show-account":
            with Storage(args.database) as storage:
                result = AccountService(storage).show_account(args.account_id)
            _print_json(result)
        elif args.command == "serve":
            return _serve(args)
        else:  # pragma: no cover - argparse enforces valid choices
            parser.error(f"unknown command {args.command!r}")
    except AccountServiceError as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


def _serve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    with Storage(args.database) as storage:
        service = AccountService(
            storage, mail_endpoint=args.mail_endpoint, recovery_ttl_seconds=args.recovery_ttl_seconds
        )
        server = create_server(args.host, args.port, service, args.bearer_token)
        bound_host, bound_port = server.server_address[:2]
        print(f"serving on http://{bound_host}:{bound_port}", flush=True)
        try:
            server.serve_forever()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            pass
        finally:
            server.server_close()
    return 0


def _print_json(payload: dict) -> None:
    print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

This all looks correct. Summary of what changed:

**New capability — configurable recovery TTL:**
- `serve --recovery-ttl-seconds SECONDS` (`accountsvc/cli.py`): positive-integer-validated via a custom argparse type (`_positive_int`), default 900 (imported from `service.RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS`, single source of truth). Invalid values are rejected by argument parsing itself, before `Storage`/`AccountService`/the HTTP server are ever constructed.
- `AccountService.__init__` (`accountsvc/service.py`) now takes `recovery_ttl_seconds`, defensively re-validated, and `start_recovery` uses it only when assigning a new token's expiry — nothing else reads it, so it never affects previously-persisted tokens.
- Expiry continues to be persisted as an absolute UTC timestamp in `recovery_requests.expires_at` and checked purely against wall-clock time on every `complete_recovery` call, so any process that reopens the database enforces it independent of which TTL that process was started with.

**Bug found and fixed:** `provider_receipts.receipt_id` was a primary key, but a receipt is provider-controlled opaque data with no uniqueness guarantee — two attempts getting the same receipt string (which the new two-process test triggered immediately) crashed the server mid-request with `sqlite3.IntegrityError`. Changed to a surrogate `id` primary key with `receipt_id` as an indexed, non-unique column.

**New tests (56 total, all passing):**
- `FailurePersistenceTests` — asserts a failed attempt persists the trusted account binding, original recipient, and `encode_retry_locator` output, including a check that a *freshly reopened* `Storage` handle can resolve the locator via the notice helpers, without invoking retry.
- `test_complete_recovery_ordinary_success` — isolated ordinary-completion case.
- `MailboxUniquenessTests` — duplicate current mailbox, cross-account collision on change, and same-address-in-different-orgs allowed.
- `RecoveryTtlConfigurationTests` — default value, rejection of non-positive/non-integer TTLs, and that a custom TTL produces the correct persisted absolute expiry.
- `tests/test_recovery_ttl_two_process.py` — spawns a real `serve --recovery-ttl-seconds 2` subprocess, creates two tokens, completes one, kills the process, sleeps past expiry, starts a second `serve` subprocess (different TTL) on the same database file, and confirms it refuses both the expired token and a replay of the completed one.

No changes were made to retry behavior — existing retry code and tests were left untouched, and the new persistence tests deliberately stop short of calling retry.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent

The conversation had three real user requests, with intent changing over time:

- Initial product request: build the starter’s standard-library account recovery service using `accountsvc`, SQLite, documented CLI commands, and loopback HTTP routes. The service had to model organizations, accounts, current/released mailbox ownership, MFA, recovery requests, opaque provider receipts, and delivery attempts. It also had to preserve the exact starter signatures for `encode_retry_locator`, `account_id_from_retry_locator`, and `recipient_from_retry_locator`, enforce organization scope, current-mailbox uniqueness, authenticated administration, bounded input, durable reads, and add lakeshore migration fixtures/tests.
- Maintenance request: inspect every file under `maintenance/inputs/provider-s03/mailbox-inventory/`, reading each completely and using separate read-only commands to record file type, line count, SHA-256, and comparisons. Write only the maintenance report, keep it separate from product code/tests, and do not modify any application artifact.
- Latest product request: add random opaque recovery tokens, bind them to one account and organization, deliver only to the current mailbox, persist failed delivery state and notice-helper output, enforce expiry and single use, but do not add/change retry behavior. Add `serve --recovery-ttl-seconds SECONDS`, default 900, reject non-positive values before database binding, persist absolute expiry in SQLite, enforce expiry after a fresh process restart, and add a real two-process test using TTL 2.

The latest request was completed. Existing retry functionality from the earlier product implementation was intentionally left unchanged; the new persistence tests did not invoke retry.

2. Key Technical Concepts

Product architecture:

- Python standard library only: `sqlite3`, `http.server`, `urllib.request`, `argparse`, `secrets`, `datetime`, `json`, and related standard modules.
- `Storage` owns a SQLite connection. It enables:
  - `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`
  - `PRAGMA synchronous=FULL`
  - `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`
  - explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / `COMMIT` transactions for writes
  - `check_same_thread=False`, because the HTTP server may serve from a different thread than the thread that opened the connection. The server is the non-threaded `HTTPServer`, so only one request uses the connection at a time.
- SQLite tables:
  - `organizations`
  - `accounts`
  - `mfa_factors`
  - `mailbox_ownership`
  - `recovery_requests`
  - `delivery_attempts`
  - `provider_receipts`
- Current mailbox uniqueness is enforced by a partial unique index:
  `UNIQUE (organization_id, email) WHERE released_at IS NULL`.
  Released addresses can be claimed by another account in the same organization.
- Recovery lookup is organization-scoped and only joins current mailbox ownership. A released address cannot initiate recovery.
- Recovery tokens are random opaque values generated with `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, persisted in `recovery_requests.recovery_token`, bound to the account and organization selected at start, and never returned in the recovery-start response.
- Recovery token lifetime:
  - `RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 900`
  - `AccountService` accepts `recovery_ttl_seconds`
  - constructor rejects non-integer, boolean, zero, and negative values with `ValidationError`
  - CLI parser validates the option before `_serve`, `Storage`, or the HTTP server are created
  - `start_recovery` uses the configured value only to calculate the expiry of a newly created token
  - the resulting absolute UTC timestamp is persisted in `recovery_requests.expires_at`
  - completion checks the persisted timestamp, not the current process’s configured TTL, so a fresh process with a different TTL still enforces the original expiry
  - comparison in `complete_recovery` is `request["expires_at"] < _now()`, using second-resolution UTC timestamps in `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` format
- Completion is single-use: only a pending, unexpired request can complete; successful completion changes `status` to `completed` and stores `completed_at`.
- Delivery sends JSON to the configured mail endpoint:
  `{"recipient": recipient, "recovery_token": recovery_token}`.
- Failed delivery persists:
  - trusted `account_id`
  - original recipient
  - failed outcome
  - `encode_retry_locator(...)` output
  - provider receipt in `provider_receipts`
- Provider receipt data is opaque and provider-controlled. `provider_receipts.receipt_id` is therefore indexed but not unique; the table uses a surrogate integer `id` primary key.
- The exact starter notice helpers remain unchanged:
  - `encode_retry_locator(receipt: str, account_id: str) -> str`
  - `account_id_from_retry_locator(saved: str, fallback_account_id: str) -> str`
  - `recipient_from_retry_locator(saved: str, stored_recipient: str, current_email: str) -> str`
- Their starter behavior is:
  - `encode_retry_locator` returns `account_id`
  - `account_id_from_retry_locator` returns `fallback_account_id`
  - `recipient_from_retry_locator` returns `current_email`
- HTTP routes:
  - `POST /recovery/start`
  - `POST /recovery/complete`
  - existing authenticated `POST /recovery/notifications/retry`
- HTTP security/limits:
  - loopback host only: `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, or `localhost`
  - retry route requires `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`
  - bearer comparison uses `hmac.compare_digest`
  - request bodies are capped at `16 * 1024` bytes before JSON parsing
- CLI:
  - `create-account`
  - `change-email`
  - `show-account`
  - `serve`
  - stable original command shapes remain intact; `--recovery-ttl-seconds` is an optional addition to `serve`
- MFA is represented by `mfa_factors.enabled` and can be set through the service layer. The recovery completion path does not independently require an MFA factor; the initial requirement was to model MFA state.

Maintenance analysis:

- Four mailbox-inventory files were discovered and read completely.
- Evidence sources agree for cases `provider-s03-t02-000001` through `000005`.
- The CSV alone contains `provider-s03-t02-000006` with `windows-x86_64 / supported`.
- The report deliberately leaves source authority for the sixth case unresolved rather than inferring it.

- `accountsvc/notice.py`
- `docs/provider-s03-contract.md`

  - Defines `AccountServiceError`, `ValidationError`, `NotFoundError`, `ConflictError`, and `AuthError`.
- `accountsvc/validation.py`

1	"""Business logic tying storage, delivery, and the retry notice together.
2	
3	This is the only layer that calls into :mod:`accountsvc.notice`. Its job is
4	to keep the recovery token bound to the account and organization captured at
5	recovery start, and to make sure a retried delivery always re-resolves the
6	account's *current* mailbox rather than trusting a previously stored value.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
11	from typing import Optional
12	
13	from . import mailer, tokens, validation
14	from .errors import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationError
15	from .notice import (
16	    account_id_from_retry_locator,
17	    encode_retry_locator,
18	    recipient_from_retry_locator,
19	)
20	from .storage import Storage
21	
22	RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 15 * 60
23	_TIME_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"
24	
25	
26	def _now() -> str:
27	    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(_TIME_FORMAT)
28	
29

"""Business logic tying storage, delivery, and the retry notice together.

This is the only layer that calls into :mod:`accountsvc.notice`. Its job is
to keep the recovery token bound to the account and organization captured at
recovery start, and to make sure a retried delivery always re-resolves the
account's *current* mailbox rather than trusting a previously stored value.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Optional

from . import mailer, tokens, validation
from .errors import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationError
from .notice import (
    account_id_from_retry_locator,
    encode_retry_locator,
    recipient_from_retry_locator,
)
from .storage import Storage

RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 15 * 60
_TIME_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(_TIME_FORMAT)


def _add_seconds(timestamp: str, seconds: int) -> str:
    when = datetime.strptime(timestamp, _TIME_FORMAT).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return (when + timedelta(seconds=seconds)).strftime(_TIME_FORMAT)


class AccountService:
    """Facade used by both the CLI and the loopback HTTP server."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        storage: Storage,
        mail_endpoint: Optional[str] = None,
        recovery_ttl_seconds: int = RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS,
    ) -> None:
        if (
            not isinstance(recovery_ttl_seconds, int)
            or isinstance(recovery_ttl_seconds, bool)
            or recovery_ttl_seconds <= 0
        ):
            raise ValidationError("recovery_ttl_seconds must be a positive integer")
        self._storage = storage
        self._mail_endpoint = mail_endpoint
        self._recovery_ttl_seconds = recovery_ttl_seconds

    # -- account administration ------------------------------------------

    def create_account(self, organization_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> dict:
        organization_id = validation.require_identifier(organization_id, "organization_id")
        account_id = validation.require_identifier(account_id, "account_id")
        email = validation.require_email(email)
        self._storage.create_account(organization_id, account_id, email, _now())
        return self.show_account(account_id)

    def change_email(self, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> dict:
        account_id = validation.require_identifier(account_id, "account_id")
        new_email = validation.require_email(new_email)
        self._storage.change_email(account_id, new_email, _now())
        return self.show_account(account_id)

    def show_account(self, account_id: str) -> dict:
        account_id = validation.require_identifier(account_id, "account_id")
        row = self._storage.require_account(account_id)
        history = self._storage.email_history(account_id)
        return {
            "account_id": row["account_id"],
            "organization_id": row["organization_id"],
            "status": row["status"],
            "mfa_enabled": self._storage.get_mfa(account_id),
            "mailbox_revision": row["mailbox_revision"],
            "current_email": self._storage.current_email(account_id),
            "email_history": [
                {
                    "email": entry["email"],
                    "claimed_at": entry["claimed_at"],
                    "released_at": entry["released_at"],
                }
                for entry in history
            ],
        }

    def set_mfa(self, account_id: str, enabled: bool) -> dict:
        account_id = validation.require_identifier(account_id, "account_id")
        self._storage.require_account(account_id)
        self._storage.set_mfa(account_id, enabled, _now())
        return self.show_account(account_id)

    # -- recovery flow -----------------------------------------------------

    def start_recovery(self, organization_id: str, email: str) -> dict:
        organization_id = validation.require_identifier(organization_id, "organization_id")
        email = validation.require_email(email)
        account = self._storage.find_account_by_org_email(organization_id, email)
        if account is None:
            raise NotFoundError("no account in this organization currently owns that email")
        account_id = account["account_id"]

        now = _now()
        request_id = tokens.new_request_id()
        recovery_token = tokens.new_recovery_token()
        expires_at = _add_seconds(now, self._recovery_ttl_seconds)
        self._storage.create_recovery_request(
            request_id, organization_id, account_id, recovery_token, now, expires_at
        )
        delivery_status = self._deliver(request_id, account_id, email, recovery_token, now)
        return {"request_id": request_id, "delivery_status": delivery_status}

    def complete_recovery(self, token: str) -> dict:
        token = validation.require_token(token)
        request = self._storage.get_recovery_request_by_token(token)
        if request is None or request["status"] != "pending" or request["expires_at"] < _now():
            raise NotFoundError("recovery token is invalid, expired, or already used")
        self._storage.complete_recovery_request(request["request_id"], _now())
        return {
            "request_id": request["request_id"],
            "account_id": request["account_id"],
            "organization_id": request["organization_id"],
            "status": "completed",
        }

    def retry_notification(self, attempt_id: int) -> dict:
        if not isinstance(attempt_id, int) or isinstance(attempt_id, bool) or attempt_id <= 0:
            raise ValidationError("delivery_attempt_id must be a positive integer")
        attempt = self._storage.get_delivery_attempt(attempt_id)
        if attempt is None:
            raise NotFoundError(f"delivery attempt {attempt_id} does not exist")
        if attempt["resolved_at"] is not None:
            raise ConflictError(f"delivery attempt {attempt_id} was already resolved")
        request = self._storage.get_recovery_request(attempt["request_id"])
        if request is None:
            raise NotFoundError(f"recovery request for attempt {attempt_id} does not exist")

        # Never trust the stored account/recipient: rebuild both from the
        # locator and the account's *current* mailbox, per contract.
        account_id = account_id_from_retry_locator(attempt["retry_locator"], attempt["account_id"])
        current_email = self._storage.current_email(account_id)
        if current_email is None:
            raise NotFoundError(f"account {account_id!r} no longer owns a current mailbox")
        recipient = recipient_from_retry_locator(attempt["retry_locator"], attempt["recipient"], current_email)

        delivery_status = self._deliver(
            request["request_id"],
            account_id,
            recipient,
            request["recovery_token"],
            _now(),
            attempt_id=attempt_id,
        )
        return {"attempt_id": attempt_id, "delivery_status": delivery_status}

    # -- delivery ------------------------------------------------------------

    def _deliver(
        self,
        request_id: str,
        account_id: str,
        recipient: str,
        recovery_token: str,
        now: str,
        attempt_id: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> str:
        if self._mail_endpoint is None:
            result = mailer.DeliveryResult(success=False, receipt=None, detail="no mail endpoint configured")
        else:
            result = mailer.send_recovery_mail(self._mail_endpoint, recipient, recovery_token)

        outcome = "success" if result.success else "failed"
        retry_locator = None if result.success else encode_retry_locator(result.receipt or "", account_id)
        resolved_at = now if result.success else None

        if attempt_id is None:
            attempt_id = self._storage.record_delivery_attempt(
                request_id, account_id, recipient, now, outcome, retry_locator, resolved_at
            )
        else:
            self._storage.resolve_delivery_attempt(attempt_id, outcome, retry_locator, resolved_at)

        receipt_id = result.receipt or tokens.new_local_receipt_id()
        self._storage.record_provider_receipt(receipt_id, attempt_id, now, result.detail)
        return "delivered" if result.success else "queued_for_retry"

1	"""SQLite-backed storage for the account recovery service.
2	
3	Models organizations, accounts, MFA state, current and released mailbox
4	ownership, recovery requests, opaque provider receipts, and delivery
5	attempts. Every write happens inside an explicit ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` /
6	``COMMIT`` transaction and the connection runs in WAL mode with
7	``synchronous=FULL`` so committed data survives a crash and is visible to
8	the next read (durable reads).
9	"""
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import sqlite3
13	from contextlib import contextmanager
14	from typing import Iterator, Optional
15	
16	from .errors import ConflictError, NotFoundError
17	
18	_SCHEMA = """
19	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS organizations (
20	    organization_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
21	    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
22	);
23	
24	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (
25	    account_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
26	    organization_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(organization_id),
27	    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
28	    mailbox_revision INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
29	    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
30	);
31	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_accounts_org ON accounts(organization_id);
32	
33	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mfa_factors (
34	    account_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
35	    enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
36	    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
37	);
38	
39	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mailbox_ownership (
40	    ownership_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
41	    organization_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(organization_id),
42	    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
43	    email TEXT NOT NULL,
44	    claimed_at TEXT NOT NULL,
45	    released_at TEXT
46	);
47	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_mailbox_current_unique
48	    ON mailbox_ownership(organization_id, email) WHERE released_at IS NULL;
49	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_mailbox_account ON mailbox_ownership(account_id);
50	
51	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recovery_requests (
52	    request_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
53	    organization_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(organization_id),
54	    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
55	    recovery_token TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
56	    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
57	    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
58	    expires_at TEXT NOT NULL,
59	    completed_at TEXT
60	);
61	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_recovery_account ON recovery_requests(account_id);
62	
63	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS delivery_attempts (
64	    attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
65	    request_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES recovery_requests(request_id),
66	    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
67	    recipient TEXT NOT NULL,
68	    attempted_at TEXT NOT NULL,
69	    outcome TEXT NOT NULL,
70	    retry_locator TEXT,
71	    retry_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
72	    resolved_at TEXT
73	);
74	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_delivery_request ON delivery_attempts(request_id);
75	
76	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS provider_receipts (
77	    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
78	    receipt_id TEXT NOT NULL,
79	    attempt_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES delivery_attempts(attempt_id),
80	    recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL,
81	    raw TEXT
82	);
83	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_receipt_attempt ON provider_receipts(attempt_id);
84	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_receipt_receipt_id ON provider_receipts(receipt_id);
85	"""
86	
87	
88	class Storage:
89	    """Owns the single SQLite connection used by the service layer."""
90	
91	    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
92	        # check_same_thread=False: the HTTP server may serve requests from a
93	        # different thread than the one that opened this connection. The
94	        # server itself is single-threaded (one request at a time), so no
95	        # two threads ever touch the connection concurrently.
96	        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=30, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)
97	        self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
98	        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
99	        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=FULL")
100	        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
101	        self._conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)
102	
103	    def close(self) -> None:
104	        self._conn.close()
105	
106	    def __enter__(self) -> "Storage":
107	        return self
108	
109	    def __exit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
110	        self.close()
111	
112	    @contextmanager
113	    def _transaction(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
114	        self._conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
115	        try:
116	            yield self._conn
117	        except Exception:
118	            self._conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
119	            raise
120	        else:
121	            self._conn.execute("COMMIT")
122	
123	    # -- organizations --------------------------------------------------
124	
125	    def ensure_organization(self, organization_id: str, now: str) -> None:
126	        with self._transaction() as conn:
127	            conn.execute(
128	                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO organizations (organization_id, created_at) VALUES (?, ?)",
129	                (organization_id, now),
130	            )
131	
132	    # -- accounts ---------------------------------------------------------
133	
134	    def create_account(self, organization_id: str, account_id: str, email: str, now: str) -> None:
135	        with self._transaction() as conn:
136	            conn.execute(
137	                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO organizations (organization_id, created_at) VALUES (?, ?)",
138	                (organization_id, now),
139	            )
140	            existing = conn.execute(
141	                "SELECT organization_id FROM accounts WHERE account_id = ?", (account_id,)
142	            ).fetchone()
143	            if existing is not None:
144	                raise ConflictError(f"account {account_id!r} already exists")
145	            conflict = conn.execute(
146	                "SELECT account_id FROM mailbox_ownership "
147	                "WHERE organization_id = ? AND email = ? AND released_at IS NULL",
148	                (organization_id, email),
149	            ).fetchone()
150	            if conflict is not None:
151	                raise ConflictError(f"email {email!r} is already owned in organization {organization_id!r}")
152	            conn.execute(
153	                "INSERT INTO accounts (account_id, organization_id, status, mailbox_revision, created_at) "
154	                "VALUES (?, ?, 'active', 1, ?)",
155	                (account_id, organization_id, now),
156	            )
157	            conn.execute(
158	                "INSERT INTO mfa_factors (account_id, enabled, updated_at) VALUES (?, 0, ?)",
159	                (account_id, now),
160	            )
161	            conn.execute(
162	                "INSERT INTO mailbox_ownership (organization_id, account_id, email, claimed_at, released_at) "
163	                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, NULL)",
164	                (organization_id, account_id, email, now),
165	            )
166	
167	    def get_account(self, account_id: str) -> Optional[sqlite3.Row]:
168	        return self._conn.execute(
169	            "SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE account_id = ?", (account_id,)
170	        ).fetchone()
171	
172	    def require_account(self, account_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row:
173	        row = self.get_account(account_id)
174	        if row is None:
175	            raise NotFoundError(f"account {account_id!r} does not exist")
176	        return row
177	
178	    def current_email(self, account_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
179	        row = self._conn.execute(
180	            "SELECT email FROM mailbox_ownership WHERE account_id = ? AND released_at IS NULL",
181	            (account_id,),
182	        ).fetchone()
183	        return row["email"] if row is not None else None
184	
185	    def get_mfa(self, account_id: str) -> bool:
186	        row = self._conn.execute(
187	            "SELECT enabled FROM mfa_factors WHERE account_id = ?", (account_id,)
188	        ).fetchone()
189	        return bool(row["enabled"]) if row is not None else False
190	
191	    def set_mfa(self, account_id: str, enabled: bool, now: str) -> None:
192	        with self._transaction() as conn:
193	            conn.execute(
194	                "INSERT INTO mfa_factors (account_id, enabled, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?) "
195	                "ON CONFLICT(account_id) DO UPDATE SET enabled = excluded.enabled, updated_at = excluded.updated_at",
196	                (account_id, int(enabled), now),
197	            )
198	
199	    def email_history(self, account_id: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
200	        return self._conn.execute(
201	            "SELECT email, claimed_at, released_at FROM mailbox_ownership "
202	            "WHERE account_id = ? ORDER BY ownership_id ASC",
203	            (account_id,),
204	        ).fetchall()
205	
206	    def change_email(self, account_id: str, new_email: str, now: str) -> None:
207	        with self._transaction() as conn:
208	            account = conn.execute(
209	                "SELECT organization_id FROM accounts WHERE account_id = ?", (account_id,)
210	            ).fetchone()
211	            if account is None:
212	                raise NotFoundError(f"account {account_id!r} does not exist")
213	            organization_id = account["organization_id"]
214	            current = conn.execute(
215	                "SELECT ownership_id, email FROM mailbox_ownership "
216	                "WHERE account_id = ? AND released_at IS NULL",
217	                (account_id,),
218	            ).fetchone()
219	            if current is not None and current["email"] == new_email:
220	                raise ConflictError(f"account {account_id!r} already owns {new_email!r}")
