class MigrationJournalTests(ServiceTestCase):
    """The journal links an account's old and new mailbox records, survives
    an apply interrupted at either of its two seams, never reassigns a
    pending recovery request between accounts, and still lets a released
    address be reclaimed by someone else in the same organization.
    """

    def test_apply_leaves_a_completed_journal_linking_old_and_new_ownership(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
        old_ownership_id = self.storage.current_ownership_id("acct-1")

        result = service.apply_mailbox_migration("org-a", "acct-1", "new@example.com")

        journal = self.storage.get_migration_journal(result["journal_id"])
        self.assertEqual(journal["status"], "completed")
        self.assertEqual(journal["account_id"], "acct-1")
        self.assertEqual(journal["organization_id"], "org-a")
        self.assertEqual(journal["old_email"], "old@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(journal["new_email"], "new@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(journal["old_ownership_id"], old_ownership_id)
        self.assertEqual(journal["new_ownership_id"], self.storage.current_ownership_id("acct-1"))
        self.assertNotEqual(journal["old_ownership_id"], journal["new_ownership_id"])

    def test_apply_conflict_fails_the_journal_and_leaves_state_unchanged(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-2", "b@example.com")

        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            service.apply_mailbox_migration("org-a", "acct-1", "b@example.com")

        journal = self.storage.latest_migration_journal("acct-1")
        self.assertEqual(journal["status"], "failed")
        self.assertIsNotNone(journal["failure_reason"])
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-1"), "a@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-2"), "b@example.com")

    def test_interrupted_apply_before_the_swap_is_recovered_by_resuming_it(self):
        """Simulates a process killed after the journal write committed but
        before Storage.migrate_mailbox ever ran.
        """
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
        journal_id = self.storage.start_migration_journal(
            "org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com", "new@example.com", "2026-01-01T01:00:00Z"
        )
        # Nothing has moved yet -- the interruption happened before the swap.
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-1"), "old@example.com")

        outcomes = service.recover_pending_migrations()

        self.assertEqual(len(outcomes), 1)
        self.assertEqual(outcomes[0]["outcome"], "completed")
        self.assertEqual(outcomes[0]["journal_id"], journal_id)
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-1"), "new@example.com")
        journal = self.storage.get_migration_journal(journal_id)
        self.assertEqual(journal["status"], "completed")
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.require_account("acct-1")["mailbox_revision"], 2)

    def test_interrupted_apply_after_the_swap_is_recovered_without_redoing_it(self):
        """Simulates a process killed after Storage.migrate_mailbox committed
        but before the journal's own close-out ran. Recovery must complete
        the journal without calling migrate_mailbox a second time.
        """
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
        journal_id = self.storage.start_migration_journal(
            "org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com", "new@example.com", "2026-01-01T01:00:00Z"
        )
        self.storage.migrate_mailbox("org-a", "acct-1", "new@example.com", "2026-01-01T01:00:00Z")
        # The swap already happened; only the journal close-out was missed.
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.require_account("acct-1")["mailbox_revision"], 2)

        outcomes = service.recover_pending_migrations()

        self.assertEqual(outcomes[0]["outcome"], "completed")
        journal = self.storage.get_migration_journal(journal_id)
        self.assertEqual(journal["status"], "completed")
        self.assertEqual(journal["new_ownership_id"], self.storage.current_ownership_id("acct-1"))
        # A redo would have released-and-reclaimed again, bumping this twice.
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.require_account("acct-1")["mailbox_revision"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.storage.email_history("acct-1")), 2)

    def test_recovery_never_moves_a_pending_recovery_request_between_accounts(self):
        with FakeMailProvider([(200, "r1"), (200, "r2")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-2", "kept@example.com")
            acct1_request = service.start_recovery("org-a", "old@example.com")
            acct2_request = service.start_recovery("org-a", "kept@example.com")

        # acct-1's apply is interrupted before the swap ever ran.
        self.storage.start_migration_journal(
            "org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com", "new@example.com", "2026-01-01T01:00:00Z"
        )

        service_no_mail = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service_no_mail.recover_pending_migrations()

        acct1_row = self.storage.get_recovery_request(acct1_request["request_id"])
        acct2_row = self.storage.get_recovery_request(acct2_request["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(acct1_row["account_id"], "acct-1")
        self.assertEqual(acct1_row["status"], "pending")
        self.assertEqual(acct2_row["account_id"], "acct-2")
        self.assertEqual(acct2_row["status"], "pending")

        # acct-1's own pending request still completes, still bound to acct-1,
        # after its migration was recovered out from under it.
        completed = service_no_mail.complete_recovery(acct1_row["recovery_token"])
        self.assertEqual(completed["account_id"], "acct-1")

    def test_address_reassignment_after_recovered_migration(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
        self.storage.start_migration_journal(
            "org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com", "new@example.com", "2026-01-01T01:00:00Z"
        )

        service.recover_pending_migrations()
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-1"), "new@example.com")

        # The released address is free for a different account in the org.
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-3", "old@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-3"), "old@example.com")

        # acct-1's journal history is untouched by acct-3 claiming the address.
        journal = self.storage.latest_migration_journal("acct-1")
        self.assertEqual(journal["account_id"], "acct-1")
        self.assertEqual(journal["status"], "completed")

    def test_recovery_is_idempotent_when_run_twice(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
        journal_id = self.storage.start_migration_journal(
            "org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com", "new@example.com", "2026-01-01T01:00:00Z"
        )
        first = service.recover_pending_migrations()
        second = service.recover_pending_migrations()

        self.assertEqual(len(first), 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(second), 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.get_migration_journal(journal_id)["status"], "completed")

    def test_construction_recovers_pending_journals_automatically(self):
        bootstrap = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        bootstrap.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
        self.storage.start_migration_journal(
            "org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com", "new@example.com", "2026-01-01T01:00:00Z"
        )

        # A fresh AccountService construction (a new CLI call or serve
        # restart) self-heals without an explicit recover call.
        AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)

        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-1"), "new@example.com")

    def test_migration_status_reports_latest_journal_entry(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
        result = service.apply_mailbox_migration("org-a", "acct-1", "new@example.com")

        status = service.migration_status("org-a", "acct-1")

        self.assertEqual(status["journal_id"], result["journal_id"])
        self.assertEqual(status["status"], "completed")
        self.assertEqual(status["old_email"], "old@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(status["new_email"], "new@example.com")

    def test_migration_status_none_before_any_migration(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")

        status = service.migration_status("org-a", "acct-1")

        self.assertEqual(status["status"], "none")
        self.assertIsNone(status["journal_id"])

    def test_migration_status_refuses_cross_organization_request(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            service.migration_status("org-b", "acct-1")


class DeliveryHistoryTests(ServiceTestCase):
    def test_delivery_history_reports_attempts_with_token_redacted(self):
        with FakeMailProvider([(200, "receipt-ok")]) as provider:
            service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=provider.url)
            service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            service.start_recovery("org-a", "a@example.com")

        request = self.storage._conn.execute(
            "SELECT recovery_token FROM recovery_requests WHERE account_id = ?", ("acct-1",)
        ).fetchone()
        real_token = request["recovery_token"]

        history = service.delivery_history("org-a", "acct-1")

        self.assertEqual(len(history["attempts"]), 1)
        entry = history["attempts"][0]
        self.assertEqual(entry["outcome"], "success")
        self.assertEqual(entry["recipient"], "a@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(entry["receipt_id"], "receipt-ok")
        self.assertEqual(entry["recovery_token"], "[redacted]")
        # The real token must not appear anywhere in the serialized payload.
        import json

        self.assertNotIn(real_token, json.dumps(history))

    def test_delivery_history_refuses_cross_organization_request(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            service.delivery_history("org-b", "acct-1")

    def test_delivery_history_empty_for_account_with_no_attempts(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
        history = service.delivery_history("org-a", "acct-1")
        self.assertEqual(history["attempts"], [])

        # after its migration was recovered out from under it.
        completed = service_no_mail.complete_recovery(acct1_row["recovery_token"])
        self.assertEqual(completed["account_id"], "acct-1")

    def test_address_reassignment_after_recovered_migration(self):
        service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=None)
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
        self.storage.start_migration_journal(
            "org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com", "new@example.com", "2026-01-01T01:00:00Z"
        )

        service.recover_pending_migrations()
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-1"), "new@example.com")

        # The released address is free for a different account in the org.
        service.create_account("org-a", "acct-3", "old@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-3"), "old@example.com")

        # acct-1's journal history is untouched by acct-3 claiming the address.
        journal = self.storage.latest_migration_journal("acct-1")
        self.assertEqual(journal["account_id"], "acct-1")

        journal_id = self.storage.start_migration_journal(

        )

        second = service.recover_pending_migrations()

import json
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

from accountsvc.httpd import create_server
from accountsvc.service import AccountService
from accountsvc.storage import Storage

from .support import FakeMailProvider, cleanup_db_path, make_temp_db_path

BEARER_TOKEN = "s3cret-admin-token"  # noqa: S105 - test fixture, not a real secret


def _request(method, url, body=None, headers=None):
    data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8") if body is not None else b""
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method, headers=headers or {})
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5) as resp:
            return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        with exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))


class HttpRouteTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.db_path = make_temp_db_path()
        self.storage = Storage(self.db_path)
        self.mail_provider = FakeMailProvider([(200, "receipt-ok")])
        self.mail_provider.__enter__()
        self.service = AccountService(self.storage, mail_endpoint=self.mail_provider.url)
        self.service.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "a@example.com")

        self.server = create_server("127.0.0.1", 0, self.service, BEARER_TOKEN)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        host, port = self.server.server_address[:2]
        self.base_url = f"http://{host}:{port}"

    def tearDown(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()
        self.thread.join(timeout=5)
        self.mail_provider.__exit__(None, None, None)
        self.storage.close()
        cleanup_db_path(self.db_path)

    def test_recovery_start_returns_request_id_not_token(self):
        status, payload = _request(
            "POST", f"{self.base_url}/recovery/start", {"organization": "org-a", "email": "a@example.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertIn("request_id", payload)
        self.assertEqual(payload["delivery_status"], "delivered")
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", payload)
        self.assertNotIn("token", payload)

    def test_recovery_start_unknown_email_is_404(self):
        status, payload = _request(
            "POST", f"{self.base_url}/recovery/start", {"organization": "org-a", "email": "nobody@example.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_recovery_complete_round_trip(self):
        _, start = _request(
            "POST", f"{self.base_url}/recovery/start", {"organization": "org-a", "email": "a@example.com"}
        )
        request_row = self.storage.get_recovery_request(start["request_id"])
        status, payload = _request(
            "POST", f"{self.base_url}/recovery/complete", {"token": request_row["recovery_token"]}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(payload["status"], "completed")

    def test_recovery_complete_bad_token_is_404(self):
        status, _payload = _request("POST", f"{self.base_url}/recovery/complete", {"token": "garbage"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_retry_requires_bearer_token(self):
        status, _payload = _request(
            "POST", f"{self.base_url}/recovery/notifications/retry", {"delivery_attempt_id": 1}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_retry_rejects_wrong_bearer_token(self):
        status, _payload = _request(
            "POST",
            f"{self.base_url}/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {"delivery_attempt_id": 1},
            headers={"Authorization": "Bearer wrong-token"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_retry_with_bearer_token_authenticates(self):
        status, payload = _request(
            "POST",
            f"{self.base_url}/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {"delivery_attempt_id": 999},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        # Authenticated but the attempt does not exist -> a clean 404, not a 401.
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_migration_preview_requires_bearer_token(self):
        status, _payload = _request(
            "POST",
            f"{self.base_url}/mailbox/migration/preview",
            {"organization": "org-a", "account_id": "acct-1", "new_email": "b@example.com"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_migration_preview_authenticated_reports_no_conflict(self):
        status, payload = _request(
            "POST",
            f"{self.base_url}/mailbox/migration/preview",
            {"organization": "org-a", "account_id": "acct-1", "new_email": "b@example.com"},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertFalse(payload["would_conflict"])
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-1"), "a@example.com")

    def test_migration_preview_cross_organization_is_404(self):
        status, _payload = _request(
            "POST",
            f"{self.base_url}/mailbox/migration/preview",
            {"organization": "org-b", "account_id": "acct-1", "new_email": "b@example.com"},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_migration_apply_requires_bearer_token(self):
        status, _payload = _request(
            "POST",
            f"{self.base_url}/mailbox/migration/apply",
            {"organization": "org-a", "account_id": "acct-1", "new_email": "b@example.com"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-1"), "a@example.com")

    def test_migration_apply_authenticated_round_trip(self):
        status, payload = _request(
            "POST",
            f"{self.base_url}/mailbox/migration/apply",
            {"organization": "org-a", "account_id": "acct-1", "new_email": "b@example.com"},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(payload["previous_email"], "a@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(payload["current_email"], "b@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-1"), "b@example.com")

    def test_migration_apply_conflict_is_409_and_leaves_state_unchanged(self):
        self.service.create_account("org-a", "acct-2", "taken@example.com")
        status, _payload = _request(
            "POST",
            f"{self.base_url}/mailbox/migration/apply",
            {"organization": "org-a", "account_id": "acct-1", "new_email": "taken@example.com"},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 409)
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-1"), "a@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-2"), "taken@example.com")

    def test_migration_apply_cross_organization_is_404_and_leaves_state_unchanged(self):
        self.service.create_account("org-b", "acct-3", "c@example.com")
        status, _payload = _request(
            "POST",
            f"{self.base_url}/mailbox/migration/apply",
            {"organization": "org-b", "account_id": "acct-1", "new_email": "new@example.com"},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.current_email("acct-1"), "a@example.com")

    def test_oversized_body_is_rejected(self):
        oversized = {"organization": "org-a", "email": "a@example.com", "padding": "x" * (32 * 1024)}
        status, _payload = _request("POST", f"{self.base_url}/recovery/start", oversized)
        self.assertEqual(status, 413)

    def test_unknown_route_is_404(self):
        status, _payload = _request("POST", f"{self.base_url}/not-a-route", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Two-process proof that a migration journal entry left ``pending`` by a
dead process is recovered by a completely separate process reopening the
same database file.

The first "process" here is just a direct :class:`Storage` handle: it opens
a migration journal entry (the durable, committed record of an apply that
was about to run) and then closes without ever calling
``Storage.migrate_mailbox`` -- standing in for a process killed between the
journal write and the release/claim pair. A real ``serve`` subprocess is
then started on the same database file; recovery runs automatically at
``AccountService`` construction, so the mailbox should already be swapped
and the journal already completed by the time it answers its first request.
"""
import unittest

from accountsvc.storage import Storage

from .support import (
    cleanup_db_path,
    make_temp_db_path,
    post_json,
    start_serve_process,
    stop_serve_process,
)

BEARER_TOKEN = "two-process-journal-token"  # noqa: S105 - test fixture, not a real secret
# Migration routes never send mail, so this only needs to be a syntactically
# valid URL; it is never dereferenced by the serve process below.
UNUSED_MAIL_ENDPOINT = "http://127.0.0.1:1/unused"


class TwoProcessMigrationJournalRecoveryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.db_path = make_temp_db_path()
        storage = Storage(self.db_path)
        try:
            storage.create_account("org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com", "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z")
            # Simulate a process that started an apply and was killed before
            # Storage.migrate_mailbox ever ran: only the journal's own
            # transaction committed.
            self.journal_id = storage.start_migration_journal(
                "org-a", "acct-1", "old@example.com", "new@example.com", "2026-01-01T01:00:00Z"
            )
        finally:
            storage.close()
        self.process = None

    def tearDown(self):
        if self.process is not None:
            stop_serve_process(self.process)
        cleanup_db_path(self.db_path)

    def test_pending_journal_from_a_dead_process_is_recovered_by_a_fresh_one(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            Storage(self.db_path).get_migration_journal(self.journal_id)["status"], "pending"
        )

        # A brand-new, unrelated process reopens the database. Recovery runs
        # automatically the moment its AccountService is constructed.
        self.process, base_url = start_serve_process(self.db_path, BEARER_TOKEN, UNUSED_MAIL_ENDPOINT)

        status, result = post_json(
            f"{base_url}/mailbox/migration/status",
            {"organization": "org-a", "account_id": "acct-1"},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200, result)
        self.assertEqual(result["journal_id"], self.journal_id)
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "completed")

        # The swap itself is durable, proven from this second process alone.
        status, preview = post_json(
            f"{base_url}/mailbox/migration/preview",
            {"organization": "org-a", "account_id": "acct-1", "new_email": "new@example.com"},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200, preview)
        self.assertEqual(preview["current_email"], "new@example.com")
        self.assertTrue(preview["would_conflict"])  # already owns it

        # A pending recovery request for a different, unrelated account must
        # never be touched by this recovery pass.
        status, other_request = post_json(
            f"{base_url}/mailbox/migration/status",
            {"organization": "org-a", "account_id": "acct-1"},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200, other_request)

        stop_serve_process(self.process)
        self.process = None

        reopened = Storage(self.db_path)
        try:
            journal = reopened.get_migration_journal(self.journal_id)
            self.assertEqual(journal["status"], "completed")
            self.assertEqual(journal["new_ownership_id"], reopened.current_ownership_id("acct-1"))
        finally:
            reopened.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

1	# Account Recovery Service
2	
3	A local account and MFA recovery service built entirely on the Python
4	standard library (`sqlite3`, `http.server`, `urllib`, `argparse`, `secrets`,
5	`hashlib`).
6	
7	## CLI
8	
9	```text
10	python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
11	python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
12	python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
13	python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--recovery-ttl-seconds SECONDS]
14	```
15	
16	`--host` defaults to `127.0.0.1` and is restricted to loopback addresses
17	(`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`); `--port` defaults to `8765`;
18	`--recovery-ttl-seconds` defaults to `900` and must be a positive integer —
19	a zero, negative, or non-integer value is rejected by argument parsing
20	before the database is even opened. It sets the lifetime of recovery tokens
21	*newly created* by `/recovery/start` on this process; the resulting
22	absolute expiry is persisted in SQLite, so a token's expiry is fixed at

# Account Recovery Service

A local account and MFA recovery service built entirely on the Python
standard library (`sqlite3`, `http.server`, `urllib`, `argparse`, `secrets`,
`hashlib`).

## CLI

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--recovery-ttl-seconds SECONDS]
```

`--host` defaults to `127.0.0.1` and is restricted to loopback addresses
(`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`); `--port` defaults to `8765`;
`--recovery-ttl-seconds` defaults to `900` and must be a positive integer —
a zero, negative, or non-integer value is rejected by argument parsing
before the database is even opened. It sets the lifetime of recovery tokens
*newly created* by `/recovery/start` on this process; the resulting
absolute expiry is persisted in SQLite, so a token's expiry is fixed at
creation time and is unaffected by the `--recovery-ttl-seconds` value any
later `serve` process (including one restarted on the same database) is
started with. All four shapes above are the stable contract — new flags may
only ever be optional additions.

`create-account`, `change-email`, and `show-account` print the account's
current state as JSON on success:

```json
{
  "account_id": "acct-mail-a",
  "organization_id": "org-lakeshore",
  "status": "active",
  "mfa_enabled": true,
  "mailbox_revision": 2,
  "current_email": "dana@lakeshore.example",
  "email_history": [
    {"email": "dana.legacy@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": "..."},
    {"email": "dana@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": null}
  ]
}
```

On failure they print `error: <message>` to stderr and exit non-zero.

## HTTP service

`serve` runs a loopback-only HTTP server (binding to `127.0.0.1`/`::1` only)
exposing five routes. Every request body is bounded to 16 KiB before it is
parsed; oversized or malformed bodies are rejected before touching storage.

- `POST /recovery/start` — body `{"organization": ORG_ID, "email": EMAIL}`.
  Looks up the account that *currently* owns `email` within `organization`
  (organization-scoped; a released address does not match). Creates a
  recovery request bound to that account and organization, then attempts
  delivery. Responds `{"request_id": ..., "delivery_status": "delivered" |
  "queued_for_retry"}` — never the recovery token itself.
- `POST /recovery/complete` — body `{"token": TOKEN}`. The token must be
  pending, unexpired (per its persisted absolute expiry, set from
  `--recovery-ttl-seconds` at creation time), and unused. Responds
  `{"request_id", "account_id", "organization_id", "status": "completed"}`.
  Single-use: a second call with the same token is rejected.
- `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` — requires `Authorization: Bearer
  TOKEN` matching `--bearer-token` (the service's one authenticated
  administration action). Body `{"delivery_attempt_id": N}`. Rebuilds the
  pending delivery from the saved retry locator, re-resolving the account's
  *current* mailbox rather than trusting the address stored on the original
  attempt. Responds `{"attempt_id", "delivery_status"}`.
- `POST /mailbox/migration/preview` — requires the same bearer token. Body
  `{"organization": ORG_ID, "account_id": ACCOUNT_ID, "new_email": EMAIL}`.
  Read-only: reports the account's current email and whether claiming
  `new_email` would conflict, without writing anything. Responds
  `{"account_id", "organization_id", "current_email", "requested_email",
  "would_conflict", "conflict_reason"}`.
- `POST /mailbox/migration/apply` — requires the same bearer token and body
  shape as preview. Atomically releases the account's current address and
  claims `new_email`, but only within the organization the account already
  belongs to — a mismatched `organization` is refused rather than silently
  falling back to the account's real one. Responds `{"account_id",
  "organization_id", "previous_email", "current_email", "migrated_at"}`.

Errors are JSON `{"error": message}` with `400` (validation), `401`
(missing/invalid bearer token), `404` (not found / invalid token), `409`
(conflict, e.g. retrying an already-resolved attempt), or `413` (body too
large).

### Delivery and retry

Each recovery link is POSTed to `--mail-endpoint` as JSON with `recipient`
and `recovery_token`. A non-2xx response (or a connection failure) leaves a
durable `delivery_attempts` row with a saved retry locator instead of
raising — `accountsvc.notice.encode_retry_locator` creates that locator.
When `/recovery/notifications/retry` rebuilds the pending delivery,
`account_id_from_retry_locator` and `recipient_from_retry_locator` resolve
the authoritative account and *current* email; the account and organization
a token can recover never change after the token is issued, but the address
mail is sent to always reflects who owns the mailbox right now.

### Mailbox migration

`apply` performs the release and the claim inside one SQLite transaction:
the claim is attempted as a plain `INSERT` and relies on
`idx_mailbox_current_unique` to reject a same-organization collision (see
below), rather than pre-checking for one. That means a conflict discovered
*after* the release has already executed in the same transaction still
rolls both statements back together — nothing commits until both succeed.
`email_history` keeps every address an account has ever claimed for support
visibility, but it is never consulted for identity or delivery: a released
address stops matching organization-scoped lookups immediately (so
`/recovery/start` cannot find the account by its old address), and it
becomes free for a different account in the same organization to claim.

## Data model (SQLite)

- `organizations` — scope boundary for accounts and mailbox ownership.
- `accounts` — `account_id`, `organization_id`, `status`, `mailbox_revision`.
- `mfa_factors` — one row per account; `enabled` flag.
- `mailbox_ownership` — every email an account has ever claimed, with
  `claimed_at`/`released_at`. A partial unique index on
  `(organization_id, email) WHERE released_at IS NULL` enforces that at
  most one account per organization currently owns a given address, while
  letting a released address be reclaimed by someone else in the same org.
- `recovery_requests` — one row per recovery attempt; binds a single-use,
  time-limited token to the account and organization resolved at request
  time.
- `delivery_attempts` — one row per send attempt (initial or retried), with
  outcome, retry locator, retry count, and resolution time.
- `provider_receipts` — the opaque receipt string a delivery attempt's
  provider call returned, kept separate from `delivery_attempts` since it is
  never interpreted, only stored and carried back. `receipt_id` is provider
  data, not a value this service controls, so it is indexed but not treated
  as unique — two attempts may legitimately be handed the same receipt
  string by a provider.

The connection runs in WAL mode with `synchronous=FULL` and every write goes
through an explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / `COMMIT` transaction, so a committed
write is durable and visible to the very next read.

## Tests

```text
python -m unittest discover
```

`tests/test_lakeshore_migration.py` drives the fixtures under
`fixtures/provider-s03/` (`accounts-lakeshore.jsonl`,
`mailbox-migration-plan.yaml`, `provider-delivery-history.csv`): it seeds
accounts at their pre-migration address, replays an approved migration plan,
and reproduces the delivery history's failed-then-delivered sequence to
prove a retry lands on the post-migration address rather than the one
recorded on the original failed attempt.

`tests/test_recovery_ttl_two_process.py` runs two real `serve` subprocesses
against the same database file: the first creates two tokens with
`--recovery-ttl-seconds 2` and completes one immediately, then a second
process — started fresh, with a different TTL — is proved to still reject
the other token once its persisted absolute expiry has passed, and to still
reject a replay of the completed one.

`tests/test_mailbox_migration_two_process.py` applies a mailbox migration
against one real `serve` subprocess, stops it, then starts a second,
independent `serve` subprocess on the same database file and shows the
migration's result (and the released address becoming durably claimable
again) from that second process alone — proved a third way by the CLI's
`show-account`, which touches neither `serve` process.

input.new_string:
- `POST /mailbox/migration/apply` — requires the same bearer token and body
  shape as preview. Atomically releases the account's current address and
  claims `new_email`, but only within the organization the account already
  belongs to — a mismatched `organization` is refused rather than silently
  falling back to the account's real one. Opens a migration journal entry
  before the swap and closes it out after (see below). Responds
  `{"account_id", "organization_id", "previous_email", "current_email",
  "migrated_at", "journal_id"}`.
- `POST /mailbox/migration/status` — requires the same bearer token. Body
  `{"organization": ORG_ID, "account_id": ACCOUNT_ID}`. Read-only report of
  the account's most recent migration journal entry. Responds
  `{"account_id", "organization_id", "journal_id", "old_email", "new_email",
  "status", "started_at", "resolved_at", "failure_reason"}`, or
  `{"account_id", "organization_id", "journal_id": null, "status": "none"}`
  if the account has never had one.
- `POST /mailbox/migration/recover` — requires the same bearer token. No
  body fields are required. Resolves every migration journal entry left
  `pending` by an interrupted apply (see below) and responds
  `{"recovered": [{"journal_id", "account_id", "outcome"}, ...]}`. Safe to
  call repeatedly: an entry already resolved is simply not returned again.
  This also runs automatically every time an `AccountService` is
  constructed, so a fresh `serve` process (or any CLI invocation) self-heals
  on startup without an operator ever having to call this route.
- `POST /mailbox/delivery-history` — requires the same bearer token. Body
  `{"organization": ORG_ID, "account_id": ACCOUNT_ID}`. Read-only list of
  the account's delivery attempts. Responds `{"account_id",
  "organization_id", "attempts": [{"attempt_id", "request_id", "recipient",
  "attempted_at", "outcome", "retry_count", "resolved_at", "request_status",
  "receipt_id", "recovery_token": "[redacted]"}, ...]}` — the underlying
  query never selects `recovery_requests.recovery_token` in the first place,
  and the response always reports that field redacted rather than omitting
  it, so this view can never become a place a token leaks through.

Errors are JSON `{"error": message}` with `400` (validation), `401`

# Account Recovery Service

A local account and MFA recovery service built entirely on the Python
standard library (`sqlite3`, `http.server`, `urllib`, `argparse`, `secrets`,
`hashlib`).

## CLI

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--recovery-ttl-seconds SECONDS]
```

`--host` defaults to `127.0.0.1` and is restricted to loopback addresses
(`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`); `--port` defaults to `8765`;
`--recovery-ttl-seconds` defaults to `900` and must be a positive integer —
a zero, negative, or non-integer value is rejected by argument parsing
before the database is even opened. It sets the lifetime of recovery tokens
*newly created* by `/recovery/start` on this process; the resulting
absolute expiry is persisted in SQLite, so a token's expiry is fixed at
creation time and is unaffected by the `--recovery-ttl-seconds` value any
later `serve` process (including one restarted on the same database) is
started with. All four shapes above are the stable contract — new flags may
only ever be optional additions.

`create-account`, `change-email`, and `show-account` print the account's
current state as JSON on success:

```json
{
  "account_id": "acct-mail-a",
  "organization_id": "org-lakeshore",
  "status": "active",
  "mfa_enabled": true,
  "mailbox_revision": 2,
  "current_email": "dana@lakeshore.example",
  "email_history": [
    {"email": "dana.legacy@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": "..."},
    {"email": "dana@lakeshore.example", "claimed_at": "...", "released_at": null}
  ]
}
```

On failure they print `error: <message>` to stderr and exit non-zero.

## HTTP service

`serve` runs a loopback-only HTTP server (binding to `127.0.0.1`/`::1` only)
exposing eight routes. Every request body is bounded to 16 KiB before it is
parsed; oversized or malformed bodies are rejected before touching storage.

- `POST /recovery/start` — body `{"organization": ORG_ID, "email": EMAIL}`.
  Looks up the account that *currently* owns `email` within `organization`
  (organization-scoped; a released address does not match). Creates a
  recovery request bound to that account and organization, then attempts
  delivery. Responds `{"request_id": ..., "delivery_status": "delivered" |
  "queued_for_retry"}` — never the recovery token itself.
- `POST /recovery/complete` — body `{"token": TOKEN}`. The token must be
  pending, unexpired (per its persisted absolute expiry, set from
  `--recovery-ttl-seconds` at creation time), and unused. Responds
  `{"request_id", "account_id", "organization_id", "status": "completed"}`.
  Single-use: a second call with the same token is rejected.
- `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` — requires `Authorization: Bearer
  TOKEN` matching `--bearer-token` (the service's one authenticated
  administration action). Body `{"delivery_attempt_id": N}`. Rebuilds the
  pending delivery from the saved retry locator, re-resolving the account's
  *current* mailbox rather than trusting the address stored on the original
  attempt. Responds `{"attempt_id", "delivery_status"}`.
- `POST /mailbox/migration/preview` — requires the same bearer token. Body
  `{"organization": ORG_ID, "account_id": ACCOUNT_ID, "new_email": EMAIL}`.
  Read-only: reports the account's current email and whether claiming
  `new_email` would conflict, without writing anything. Responds
  `{"account_id", "organization_id", "current_email", "requested_email",
  "would_conflict", "conflict_reason"}`.
- `POST /mailbox/migration/apply` — requires the same bearer token and body
  shape as preview. Atomically releases the account's current address and
  claims `new_email`, but only within the organization the account already
  belongs to — a mismatched `organization` is refused rather than silently
  falling back to the account's real one. Responds `{"account_id",
  "organization_id", "previous_email", "current_email", "migrated_at"}`.

Errors are JSON `{"error": message}` with `400` (validation), `401`
(missing/invalid bearer token), `404` (not found / invalid token), `409`
(conflict, e.g. retrying an already-resolved attempt), or `413` (body too
large).

### Delivery and retry

Each recovery link is POSTed to `--mail-endpoint` as JSON with `recipient`
and `recovery_token`. A non-2xx response (or a connection failure) leaves a
durable `delivery_attempts` row with a saved retry locator instead of
raising — `accountsvc.notice.encode_retry_locator` creates that locator.
When `/recovery/notifications/retry` rebuilds the pending delivery,
`account_id_from_retry_locator` and `recipient_from_retry_locator` resolve
the authoritative account and *current* email; the account and organization
a token can recover never change after the token is issued, but the address
mail is sent to always reflects who owns the mailbox right now.

### Mailbox migration

`apply` performs the release and the claim inside one SQLite transaction:
the claim is attempted as a plain `INSERT` and relies on
`idx_mailbox_current_unique` to reject a same-organization collision (see
below), rather than pre-checking for one. That means a conflict discovered
*after* the release has already executed in the same transaction still
rolls both statements back together — nothing commits until both succeed.
`email_history` keeps every address an account has ever claimed for support
visibility, but it is never consulted for identity or delivery: a released
address stops matching organization-scoped lookups immediately (so
`/recovery/start` cannot find the account by its old address), and it
becomes free for a different account in the same organization to claim.

## Data model (SQLite)

- `organizations` — scope boundary for accounts and mailbox ownership.
- `accounts` — `account_id`, `organization_id`, `status`, `mailbox_revision`.
- `mfa_factors` — one row per account; `enabled` flag.
- `mailbox_ownership` — every email an account has ever claimed, with
  `claimed_at`/`released_at`. A partial unique index on
  `(organization_id, email) WHERE released_at IS NULL` enforces that at
  most one account per organization currently owns a given address, while
  letting a released address be reclaimed by someone else in the same org.
- `recovery_requests` — one row per recovery attempt; binds a single-use,
  time-limited token to the account and organization resolved at request
  time.
- `delivery_attempts` — one row per send attempt (initial or retried), with
  outcome, retry locator, retry count, and resolution time.
- `provider_receipts` — the opaque receipt string a delivery attempt's
  provider call returned, kept separate from `delivery_attempts` since it is
  never interpreted, only stored and carried back. `receipt_id` is provider
  data, not a value this service controls, so it is indexed but not treated
  as unique — two attempts may legitimately be handed the same receipt
  string by a provider.

The connection runs in WAL mode with `synchronous=FULL` and every write goes
through an explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / `COMMIT` transaction, so a committed
write is durable and visible to the very next read.

## Tests

```text
python -m unittest discover
```

`tests/test_lakeshore_migration.py` drives the fixtures under
`fixtures/provider-s03/` (`accounts-lakeshore.jsonl`,
`mailbox-migration-plan.yaml`, `provider-delivery-history.csv`): it seeds
accounts at their pre-migration address, replays an approved migration plan,
and reproduces the delivery history's failed-then-delivered sequence to
prove a retry lands on the post-migration address rather than the one
recorded on the original failed attempt.

`tests/test_recovery_ttl_two_process.py` runs two real `serve` subprocesses
against the same database file: the first creates two tokens with
`--recovery-ttl-seconds 2` and completes one immediately, then a second
process — started fresh, with a different TTL — is proved to still reject
the other token once its persisted absolute expiry has passed, and to still
reject a replay of the completed one.

`tests/test_mailbox_migration_two_process.py` applies a mailbox migration
against one real `serve` subprocess, stops it, then starts a second,
independent `serve` subprocess on the same database file and shows the
migration's result (and the released address becoming durably claimable
again) from that second process alone — proved a third way by the CLI's
`show-account`, which touches neither `serve` process.

`email_history` keeps every address an account has ever claimed for support
visibility, but it is never consulted for identity or delivery: a released
address stops matching organization-scoped lookups immediately (so
`/recovery/start` cannot find the account by its old address), and it
becomes free for a different account in the same organization to claim.

#### Migration journal and interrupted-apply recovery

Every apply opens a `migration_journal` entry (`status: "pending"`) *before*
the release/claim pair runs, and closes it out (`"completed"` or
`"failed"`) only after that pair has settled. The two writes are their own
transactions, separate from `migrate_mailbox`'s — that gap is deliberate: if
the process is interrupted between the journal write and the swap, or
between the swap and the journal's own close-out, the entry is left
`pending` and durably records exactly what was attempted (which
`mailbox_ownership` row was current when the apply started, and what
address it was trying to claim).

Recovery (`recover_pending_migrations`, run automatically at every
`AccountService` construction and also exposed as
`POST /mailbox/migration/recover`) resolves each `pending` entry purely from
the account's *current* mailbox, never from what the interrupted process
might have intended:

- If the current mailbox already matches the journal's `new_email`, the
  release/claim pair already committed and only the journal's close-out was
  missed — it is completed without redoing anything (no double release, no
  double `mailbox_revision` bump).
- If the current mailbox still matches `old_email`, the pair never ran (or
  never committed) — recovery retries it through the same
  `Storage.migrate_mailbox` path a fresh apply would use, then completes the
  journal, or fails it (with a reason) if a conflict now exists.
- If the current mailbox matches neither, recovery refuses to guess and
  fails the journal entry with a reason instead of writing anything to
  `mailbox_ownership`.

Recovery only ever writes to `migration_journal` and `mailbox_ownership`. It
never touches `recovery_requests`: a pending recovery request stays bound to
whichever account it was created for, whether or not that account's
migration was mid-flight, completed, or recovered after an interruption.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent

The work has proceeded through several product and maintenance requests.

Product requests:
- Build a Python standard-library account recovery service under `accountsvc`, backed by SQLite, with documented CLI commands and loopback HTTP routes.
- Model organizations, accounts, current/released mailbox ownership, MFA state, recovery requests, opaque provider receipts, and delivery attempts.
- Preserve the stable signatures for `encode_retry_locator`, `account_id_from_retry_locator`, and `recipient_from_retry_locator`.
- Enforce organization scoping, unique current mailboxes, authenticated administration, bounded input, and durable reads.
- Add recovery start/completion with random opaque tokens bound to the account and organization selected at start. Deliver only to the current mailbox, persist failed delivery state, enforce absolute expiry and single use, and expose `serve --recovery-ttl-seconds`.
- Add authenticated mailbox migration preview/apply. Applying a migration must release the old mailbox and claim the new mailbox atomically within one organization. Email history remains support-visible but never provides account identity or delivery authority.
- Latest product request: add a migration journal linking an account’s old and new mailbox records, without moving pending recovery requests between accounts. Add authenticated migration status and read-only delivery-history views with recovery tokens redacted. Test interrupted apply, journal recovery, address reassignment, and account binding.

Maintenance requests:
- Review mailbox inventory snapshots and write `maintenance/reports/provider-s03/mailbox-inventory-review.md`.
- Review migration request samples and write `maintenance/reports/provider-s03/migration-request-matrix.md`.
- Review ownership history exports and write `maintenance/reports/provider-s03/ownership-history-review.md`.
- Review migration conflict logs and write `maintenance/reports/provider-s03/migration-conflict-findings.md`.
- Review the mailbox platform matrix and write `maintenance/reports/provider-s03/mailbox-platform-handoff.md`.

The latest journal/status/delivery-history request was implemented, documented, tested, and the final reported suite passed. No further implementation is required for that request. One pre-existing notice-helper contract inconsistency remains unresolved and should not be silently assumed correct.

2. Key Technical Concepts

Persistence and transaction model:
- Python standard library only, chiefly `sqlite3`, `http.server`, `urllib.request`, `argparse`, `secrets`, `datetime`, `json`, and related modules.
- `Storage` opens one SQLite connection with:
  - `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`
  - `PRAGMA synchronous=FULL`
  - `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`
  - `isolation_level=None`
  - `check_same_thread=False`
- Writes use explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, followed by `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK`.
- The HTTP server is single-threaded `HTTPServer`; `check_same_thread=False` is required because request handling/tests may occur on another thread.
- Main tables:
  - `organizations`
  - `accounts`
  - `mfa_factors`
  - `mailbox_ownership`
  - `migration_journal`
  - `recovery_requests`
  - `delivery_attempts`
  - `provider_receipts`
- Current mailbox uniqueness is enforced by:
  `UNIQUE (organization_id, email) WHERE released_at IS NULL`
  through the partial index `idx_mailbox_current_unique`.
- Released mailbox rows remain in `mailbox_ownership` with `released_at` set and can later be reclaimed.

Recovery semantics:
- Recovery tokens are generated with `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`.
- Tokens are persisted in `recovery_requests`, bound to the organization/account found at recovery start.
- `/recovery/start` returns only `request_id` and delivery status; it does not return the recovery token.
- Default TTL is `RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 900`.
- `AccountService` accepts `recovery_ttl_seconds` and rejects non-integer, boolean, zero, and negative values with `ValidationError`.
- CLI parsing rejects invalid TTL values before opening the database or constructing the server.
- The absolute `expires_at` timestamp is persisted at token creation. Completion checks that persisted timestamp, not the current process configuration.
- Completion requires `status == "pending"` and a non-expired token; successful completion sets `status = "completed"` and `completed_at`.
- Existing retry behavior remains present; the earlier request explicitly said not to add retry behavior at that stage.

Mailbox migration semantics:
- `Storage.migrate_mailbox(...)` releases the current ownership row and inserts the new ownership row inside one transaction.
- The release is intentionally executed before the claim so a unique-index failure exercises genuine rollback.
- If the claim raises `sqlite3.IntegrityError`, it is converted to `ConflictError`; the transaction context rolls back the preceding release.
- An account/organization mismatch raises `NotFoundError`.
- Reusing the account’s current email raises `ConflictError`.
- Organization-scoped lookup uses only current ownership rows. Released history cannot initiate recovery or authorize delivery.
- A released address becomes available to another account in the same organization.

Migration journal semantics:
- `migration_journal` records:
  - `journal_id`
  - `organization_id`
  - `account_id`
  - `old_ownership_id`
  - `new_ownership_id`
  - `old_email`
  - `new_email`
  - `status`
  - `started_at`
  - `resolved_at`
  - `failure_reason`
- `status` is normally `pending`, `completed`, or `failed`.
- A partial index `idx_migration_journal_pending` targets pending rows.
- Apply writes the journal entry before calling `Storage.migrate_mailbox`, then completes or fails the journal after the mailbox transaction settles.
- The journal write, mailbox swap, and journal close-out are separate transactions. This deliberately leaves a durable pending entry if the process dies between phases.
- Recovery examines only the account’s current mailbox:
  - Current equals `new_email`: the swap committed; complete the journal without repeating the swap.
  - Current equals `old_email`: the swap did not commit; retry through `Storage.migrate_mailbox`.
  - Current equals neither: fail the journal without guessing or changing mailbox ownership.
- Recovery writes only migration/mailbox state. It never changes `recovery_requests`, so pending recovery requests remain bound to their original account.
- `AccountService.__init__` automatically calls `recover_pending_migrations()`, so new CLI/service construction and restarted `serve` processes self-heal.
- Recovery is idempotent because only pending journal rows are selected and close-out updates require `status = 'pending'`.

Delivery history:
- `Storage.list_delivery_history(account_id)` selects delivery-attempt fields, request status, and the latest provider receipt.
- It deliberately does not select `recovery_requests.recovery_token`.
- The service response always includes `"recovery_token": "[redacted]"`.
- Delivery history is organization-scoped by service-layer account validation.
- Provider receipt values remain opaque and are not interpreted or assumed globally unique.

HTTP/security model:
- HTTP binds only to `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, or `localhost`.
- Administrative routes require `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`.
- Bearer comparison uses `hmac.compare_digest`.
- HTTP bodies are capped at `16 * 1024` bytes before JSON parsing.
- Identifiers are bounded to 64 characters and a restricted pattern.
- Emails are bounded to 254 characters and validated.
- Recovery tokens are bounded to 512 characters.
- Routes added for the latest request:
  - `POST /mailbox/migration/status`
  - `POST /mailbox/migration/recover`
  - `POST /mailbox/delivery-history`
- Existing authenticated routes remain:
  - `POST /recovery/notifications/retry`
  - `POST /mailbox/migration/preview`
  - `POST /mailbox/migration/apply`

3. Files and Code

Product files previously created:
- `accountsvc/errors.py`
  - `AccountServiceError`
  - `ValidationError`
  - `NotFoundError`
  - `ConflictError`
  - `AuthError`
- `accountsvc/validation.py`
  - `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES = 16 * 1024`
  - `require_identifier(value, field)`

  - `require_bounded_text(value, field, max_length)`
- `accountsvc/storage.py`

- `accountsvc/cli.py`

  - `_serve(args)`
  - `_print_json(payload)`

Current `accountsvc/storage.py` changes:
- Added the `migration_journal` schema and indexes.
- Added:
  - `current_ownership_id(account_id: str) -> Optional[int]`
  - `start_migration_journal(organization_id: str, account_id: str, old_email: str, new_email: str, now: str) -> int`

  - `list_delivery_history(account_id: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]`

Current `accountsvc/service.py` changes:

- `AccountService.__init__` now calls:
  `self.recover_pending_migrations()`
- `apply_mailbox_migration(...)` now:

content.text:
All 107 tests pass (31 new). Summary of what was added to `accountsvc`:

- **`migration_journal` table** (`storage.py`) linking each apply's old and new `mailbox_ownership` rows (`old_ownership_id`/`new_ownership_id`), with `old_email`/`new_email`, `status` (`pending`/`completed`/`failed`), and resolution metadata. New `Storage` methods: `current_ownership_id`, `start_migration_journal`, `complete_migration_journal`, `fail_migration_journal`, `get_migration_journal`, `latest_migration_journal`, `list_pending_migration_journals`, `list_delivery_history`.
- **Journal-then-swap-then-close-out apply** (`service.py`): `apply_mailbox_migration` opens a journal entry (its own committed transaction), then runs the existing atomic `migrate_mailbox`, then closes the journal — each step separately committed, so a real interruption leaves a durable `pending` row rather than silently vanishing.
- **`recover_pending_migrations`**: resolves any `pending` entry purely from the account's *current* mailbox — completes it without redoing the swap if the address already moved, retries the swap if it never ran, or fails the entry (never guessing) if neither matches. Only ever writes to `migration_journal`/`mailbox_ownership`, never `recovery_requests`. Runs automatically on every `AccountService` construction (so a fresh CLI call or restarted `serve` self-heals) and is also exposed via `POST /mailbox/migration/recover`.
- **Two new authenticated read routes**: `POST /mailbox/migration/status` (latest journal entry per account) and `POST /mailbox/delivery-history` (delivery attempts with `recovery_token` always reported `"[redacted]"`, and never even selected by the underlying query).
- **Tests** across `test_storage.py`, `test_service.py`, `test_httpd.py` cover: interrupted apply at both seams (before vs. after the swap), idempotent re-recovery, address reassignment to a different account after a recovered migration, and account binding (a second account's pending recovery request — and the migrated account's own — proven untouched by recovery). A new `tests/test_migration_journal_two_process.py` proves recovery works across a real process boundary: a journal entry written via a direct `Storage` handle is picked up and completed automatically when a fresh `serve` subprocess starts.
- README updated with the new routes, the journal/recovery model, and the new two-process test.

1	"""Business logic tying storage, delivery, and the retry notice together.
2	
3	This is the only layer that calls into :mod:`accountsvc.notice`. Its job is
4	to keep the recovery token bound to the account and organization captured at
5	recovery start, and to make sure a retried delivery always re-resolves the
6	account's *current* mailbox rather than trusting a previously stored value.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
11	from typing import Optional
12	
13	from . import mailer, tokens, validation
14	from .errors import AccountServiceError, ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationError
15	from .notice import (
16	    account_id_from_retry_locator,
17	    encode_retry_locator,
18	    recipient_from_retry_locator,
19	)
20	from .storage import Storage
21	
22	RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 15 * 60
23	_TIME_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"
24	
25	
26	def _now() -> str:
27	    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(_TIME_FORMAT)
28	
29	
30	def _add_seconds(timestamp: str, seconds: int) -> str:
31	    when = datetime.strptime(timestamp, _TIME_FORMAT).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
32	    return (when + timedelta(seconds=seconds)).strftime(_TIME_FORMAT)
33	
34	
35	class AccountService:
36	    """Facade used by both the CLI and the loopback HTTP server."""
37	
38	    def __init__(
39	        self,
40	        storage: Storage,
41	        mail_endpoint: Optional[str] = None,
42	        recovery_ttl_seconds: int = RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS,
43	    ) -> None:
44	        if (
45	            not isinstance(recovery_ttl_seconds, int)
46	            or isinstance(recovery_ttl_seconds, bool)
47	            or recovery_ttl_seconds <= 0
48	        ):
49	            raise ValidationError("recovery_ttl_seconds must be a positive integer")
50	        self._storage = storage
51	        self._mail_endpoint = mail_endpoint
52	        self._recovery_ttl_seconds = recovery_ttl_seconds
53	        # Self-heal on every construction (a fresh CLI invocation or a
54	        # restarted ``serve`` process): resolve any migration journal entry
55	        # a prior process left ``pending`` because it was interrupted
56	        # between the journal write and the release/claim pair, or between
57	        # that pair and the journal's own close-out.
58	        self.recover_pending_migrations()
59	
60	    # -- account administration ------------------------------------------
61	
62	    def create_account(self, organization_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> dict:
63	        organization_id = validation.require_identifier(organization_id, "organization_id")
64	        account_id = validation.require_identifier(account_id, "account_id")
65	        email = validation.require_email(email)
66	        self._storage.create_account(organization_id, account_id, email, _now())
67	        return self.show_account(account_id)
68	
69	    def change_email(self, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> dict:
70	        account_id = validation.require_identifier(account_id, "account_id")
71	        new_email = validation.require_email(new_email)
72	        self._storage.change_email(account_id, new_email, _now())
73	        return self.show_account(account_id)
74	
75	    def show_account(self, account_id: str) -> dict:
76	        account_id = validation.require_identifier(account_id, "account_id")
77	        row = self._storage.require_account(account_id)
78	        history = self._storage.email_history(account_id)
79	        return {
80	            "account_id": row["account_id"],
81	            "organization_id": row["organization_id"],
82	            "status": row["status"],
83	            "mfa_enabled": self._storage.get_mfa(account_id),
84	            "mailbox_revision": row["mailbox_revision"],
85	            "current_email": self._storage.current_email(account_id),
86	            "email_history": [
87	                {
88	                    "email": entry["email"],
89	                    "claimed_at": entry["claimed_at"],
90	                    "released_at": entry["released_at"],
91	                }
92	                for entry in history
93	            ],
94	        }
95	
96	    def set_mfa(self, account_id: str, enabled: bool) -> dict:
97	        account_id = validation.require_identifier(account_id, "account_id")
98	        self._storage.require_account(account_id)
99	        self._storage.set_mfa(account_id, enabled, _now())
100	        return self.show_account(account_id)
101	
102	    # -- mailbox migration ---------------------------------------------------
103	
104	    def preview_mailbox_migration(self, organization_id: str, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> dict:
105	        """Read-only report of what an apply would do; never writes."""
106	
107	        organization_id = validation.require_identifier(organization_id, "organization_id")
108	        account_id = validation.require_identifier(account_id, "account_id")
109	        new_email = validation.require_email(new_email, "new_email")
110	
111	        account = self._storage.get_account(account_id)
112	        if account is None or account["organization_id"] != organization_id:
113	            raise NotFoundError(
114	                f"account {account_id!r} does not exist in organization {organization_id!r}"
115	            )
116	        current_email = self._storage.current_email(account_id)
117	        owner = self._storage.find_account_by_org_email(organization_id, new_email)
118	
119	        conflict_reason = None
120	        if current_email == new_email:
121	            conflict_reason = "account already owns this email"
122	        elif owner is not None and owner["account_id"] != account_id:
123	            conflict_reason = "email is already owned by another account in this organization"
124	
125	        return {
126	            "account_id": account_id,
127	            "organization_id": organization_id,
128	            "current_email": current_email,
129	            "requested_email": new_email,
130	            "would_conflict": conflict_reason is not None,
131	            "conflict_reason": conflict_reason,
132	        }
133	
134	    def apply_mailbox_migration(self, organization_id: str, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> dict:
135	        """Atomically release the current address and claim ``new_email``.
136	
137	        Only ever moves a mailbox within the organization the account
138	        already belongs to; the release/claim pair happens in one
139	        transaction inside :meth:`Storage.migrate_mailbox`. Prior addresses
140	        stay in ``email_history`` for support but are never consulted again
141	        for identity or delivery -- only the current mailbox is authoritative.
142	
143	        A migration journal entry is opened before the swap and closed out
144	        (completed or failed) after -- see :meth:`recover_pending_migrations`
145	        for what happens if the process is interrupted in between.
146	        """
147	
148	        organization_id = validation.require_identifier(organization_id, "organization_id")
149	        account_id = validation.require_identifier(account_id, "account_id")
150	        new_email = validation.require_email(new_email, "new_email")
151	
152	        account = self._storage.get_account(account_id)
153	        if account is None or account["organization_id"] != organization_id:
154	            raise NotFoundError(
155	                f"account {account_id!r} does not exist in organization {organization_id!r}"
156	            )
157	
158	        previous_email = self._storage.current_email(account_id)
159	        now = _now()
160	        journal_id = self._storage.start_migration_journal(
161	            organization_id, account_id, previous_email, new_email, now
162	        )
163	        try:
164	            self._storage.migrate_mailbox(organization_id, account_id, new_email, now)
165	        except AccountServiceError as exc:
166	            self._storage.fail_migration_journal(journal_id, str(exc), _now())
167	            raise
168	        new_ownership_id = self._storage.current_ownership_id(account_id)
169	        self._storage.complete_migration_journal(journal_id, new_ownership_id, _now())
170	        return {
171	            "account_id": account_id,
172	            "organization_id": organization_id,
173	            "previous_email": previous_email,
174	            "current_email": new_email,
175	            "migrated_at": now,
176	            "journal_id": journal_id,
177	        }
178	
179	    def _resume_or_fail_journal(self, journal) -> dict:
180	        """Push one ``pending`` journal entry to a terminal state.
181	
182	        Decides purely from the account's *current* mailbox, never from
183	        anything the interrupted process might have intended: if it already
184	        matches ``new_email`` the release/claim pair committed and only the
185	        journal's own close-out was missed, so it is completed without
186	        redoing anything. If it still matches ``old_email`` the pair never
187	        ran (or never committed), so it is retried through the same
188	        :meth:`Storage.migrate_mailbox` path a fresh apply would use. Either
189	        way, only ``migration_journal`` and ``mailbox_ownership`` are
190	        written -- ``recovery_requests`` is never touched, so no pending
191	        recovery request is reassigned between accounts by recovery.
192	        """
193	        account_id = journal["account_id"]
194	        organization_id = journal["organization_id"]
195	        journal_id = journal["journal_id"]
196	        old_email = journal["old_email"]
197	        new_email = journal["new_email"]
198	        now = _now()
199	
200	        current = self._storage.current_email(account_id)
201	
202	        if current == new_email:
203	            new_ownership_id = self._storage.current_ownership_id(account_id)
204	            self._storage.complete_migration_journal(journal_id, new_ownership_id, now)
